schema: figure variation: id, area, number, name, figure_analysis, fitting_analysis (symptoms), fabric_requirement, change_required, methods {slash, seam, pivot} (each may be null), source {book, pages}, status, reviewer. Summaries in own words.

variations.name: Long lower torso
variations.figure_analysis: Pelvic cradle is longer than average, so the distance from waist to fullest buttock is longer. Bone structure does not change the abdomen curve.
fitting_analysis: Fabric loose above the hipline at the side seams and below the back dart tips
Skirt hip fitting line stays level
Trousers: hip fitting line bows downward across the centre because fabric binds at the crotch; fabric pulls into the crotch crease or forms diagonal wrinkles from crotch to hip bones and buttocks
Hem may ride too high
variations.fabric_requirement: More length from waist to buttocks and longer back darts. Garment shaping must follow the body curve.
variations.change_required: Increase length above the hipline, or lower the curvature on the side seams.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Cut around the garment below the front dart tips, parallel to the waistline. Insert a strip and spread evenly until the shape follows the body. Adjust hem.
methods.pivot: Release side seams from waist to hipline. Take in equal amounts at back and front above the hipline. Blend into the original seamline toward waist and hip. Mark longer back dart tips. For a fitting garment, mark the new hipline. Trousers: lower the crotch seamline by a parallel new stitching line across the inseam, blend near the hip, and trim the widened seam allowance. Adjust hem.

variations.name: Short lower torso
variations.figure_analysis: Pelvic cradle is shorter than average, so the distance from waist to fullest buttock is shorter. Bone structure does not change the abdomen curve.
fitting_analysis: Fabric snug at the hipline along the side seams and across the back darts
Buttocks may lift the fabric into a horizontal fold across the back darts
Hip fitting line rises across centre back; side seams slant toward the back at the hem
Trousers: crotch seam sits below body level, inhibiting walking and straining the crotch stitching
variations.fabric_requirement: Less length from waist to buttocks and shorter back darts. Garment shaping must follow the body curve so the hip line stays level.
variations.change_required: Shorten evenly above the hipline, or raise the curvature on the side seams.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Form a parallel tuck around the whole garment below the front dart tips. Adjust tuck width evenly until the shape follows the body. Adjust hem.
methods.pivot: Pants: release the whole waistline seam; lift the garment evenly to the body curve to decrease crotch depth; clip the widened waistline allowance at 2-inch (5 cm) intervals; restore waist circumference by widening darts and taking in side seams front and back; trim; adjust hem. Skirt: release side seams from hipline to waist; let out allowances equally at back and front; blend near waist and hipline; shorten darts. Fitting garment: mark the new hip fitting line.

variations.name: Large waist
variations.figure_analysis: The waist indents less than average, through more body tissue, flaccid muscles or slumped posture.
fitting_analysis: Closing the garment compresses soft tissue at the waist, lifting the fabric into a horizontal fold around the waistline
Hip fitting line stays level but the hem rises
Trousers: the fold is smaller or absent; fabric binds at the crotch, pulling diagonal wrinkles from crotch to hip bones and pulling the hip line down at centre; crotch becomes taut and uncomfortable
variations.fabric_requirement: More fabric width at the waistline. The wider area relaxes and lowers to the correct position over the body contour. Also affects the bodice waistline (see Upper Torso 70).
variations.change_required: Widen the waistline area at the side seams.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Mark each side seam above the hipline where tightness begins. Release the waist seam across each side area. On back and front, cut through the waistline seam allowance near each side seam and continue diagonally to the side seam mark, without cutting the side seam allowance. Insert strips; spread each set equally at the waist for width; taper to nothing at the side seams. Let out waistband or bodice side seams equal to the skirt or trouser change.
methods.pivot: Release the waistline seam across each side area. Release the side seams from the waist to near the hipline. Let out allowances equally at the waist, blend near the hipline, and let out waistband or bodice side seams equal to the change.

variations.name: Small waist
variations.figure_analysis: The waist indents more than average, through less body tissue, taut muscles or an overly erect posture.
fitting_analysis: Garment opening laps past the closure line; waist, hip and hem drop below their body positions
Fabric near the side seams loose; hip fitting line level
Trousers: crotch seam sits below body level, causing strain and lowering the hemline
variations.fabric_requirement: Less fabric width at the waistline. The narrower area aligns with the waist and lifts the shaping to the body.
variations.change_required: Narrow the waistline area at the side seams.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Release the waistline seam across each side area. Near each side seam, on back and front, form a tuck through the waistline to remove the excess equally, keeping ease. Taper each tuck to nothing where the looseness ends. Take in waistband or bodice side seams equal to the skirt or trouser change.
methods.pivot: Release the waist seam and the side seams from the waist to above the hip where the variation begins. Take in side seam areas equally at the waist, blend near the hipline, trim, and take in waistband or bodice side seams equal to the change.

variations.name: Prominent hip bones
variations.figure_analysis: The upper tips of the pelvic cradle protrude more than average, through larger or more angular bone, or light, taut muscle over the area. The abdomen may look indented.
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut over the hip bones; diagonal wrinkles radiate toward the side seams and centre front
Hip fitting line may rise toward each hip bone
Slight horizontal wrinkle may form near the waistline above each bone
variations.fabric_requirement: More width and length over the hip bones. Wider front darts that may need repositioning and straighter stitching; darts nearest centre front may be unnecessary, or be made very narrow, or converted to ease or gathers. Larger areas relax and lower to the body contour, and the hip fitting line becomes level.
variations.change_required: Lengthen and widen the area over the hip bones.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Clip near the waistline halfway between centre front and each side seam. Continue cutting diagonally to the side seam just above the hipline. Insert strips; spread each set equally at the dart tips to gain width and length. Taper to nothing at the side seams and the waist. Reposition the darts if needed.
methods.pivot: Release side seams above the hipline and the waist seam above the hip bones. Reposition side darts if needed and widen them to relax the fabric over the hip bones. Let out front side-seam allowances at the waist to restore waist circumference. Blend above the hip; lower the loosened waistline until the fabric relaxes and the hip fitting line is level; blend near centre front and side seams.

variations.name: Prominent abdomen
variations.figure_analysis: Abdominal muscles lack tone, so the abdomen protrudes. Excess fatty tissue and slumped posture intensify the roundness.
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut across the abdomen; side seam above the hip curve bows forward; horizontal fold may form at the front waistline
Centre front skirt cups under the abdomen: hip line rises and hem protrudes; diagonal wrinkles pull from the abdomen to the side seams, which slant forward at the hem
Elasticised trouser waistbands curve down at centre front; fitted waistbands bind at the crotch with wrinkles to the hip bones
variations.fabric_requirement: More width and length along the whole centre front. Wider darts whose stitching lines bow toward each other. The larger area relaxes over the abdomen and eases the trouser crotch; the skirt hangs from the abdominal curve; elastic waistbands align above the curve; side seams hang plumb and the hip fitting line becomes level.
variations.change_required: Widen the midfront area; lengthen the upper centre front area.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Release the centre front seam, or slash along the centre front fold and insert a strip. To widen, spread the centre front edges evenly until the fabric relaxes over the abdomen; mark darts in their new position and shape. To increase centre front length, cut across the front just below the dart tips, insert a strip, and spread equally across the centre until the fitting line is level. Taper to nothing at each side seam.
methods.pivot: Skirt: release the front waist seam; to gain width release the centre front seam or both side seams for their full lengths; let out front seam allowances equally until the fabric relaxes across the abdomen; stitch new seamlines parallel to the originals; widen darts to restore waist circumference; mark and restitch dart shaping. Trousers: same, but widen only at centre front, letting both edges out evenly from waist to hip, blending back at the crotch curve. For more centre front length, let out the waistline seam allowance evenly across the centre front until the hip fitting line is level, and blend at the side seam. Alternatively lift the back waistline; trousers may then need more back crotch depth (see 17 Drooped Buttocks).

variations.name: Flat abdomen
variations.figure_analysis: The abdominal area is flat, through taut muscles, an overly erect posture or little fat.
fitting_analysis: Fabric loose over the abdomen; vertical folds hang below the darts nearest centre front, which create excess shaping
Hip fitting line may drop across centre front
variations.fabric_requirement: Less shaping over the abdomen. Darts nearest centre front may be removed for some figures; occasionally less length is needed at centre front. Very narrow darts stop excess shaping and keep the appearance. The smaller area lies smoothly against the body.
variations.change_required: Narrow the midfront area; shorten the upper centre front area.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. To decrease dart width and centre front length, form a parallel tuck across the centre front below the dart tips. Adjust the width until the hip fitting line is level. Taper to nothing at the side seams. Follow the crosswise grain.
methods.pivot: Release the front waistline seam and front darts; release side seams above the hipline. To decrease width, narrow the darts to smooth the fabric across the abdomen; take in front areas equally at both side seams to restore waist circumference; if needed, lift the fabric across centre front to remove excess length; trim. Trousers: release front waist seam, centre front seam and darts; narrow darts; take in excess width equally at centre front, tapering to nothing at the hipline; if needed lift evenly across centre front; blend into original side-seam stitching. With a centre-front zipper, remove the excess waist width at the side seam as for the skirt.

variations.name: Sway back
variations.figure_analysis: The pelvic cradle does not lie plumb. As the top tilts forward, the coccyx tilts outward and upward, so the buttocks protrude and the groin indents more than average. Distance from the fullest buttock to the body's central axis increases; distance from hip to waist at centre back decreases.
fitting_analysis: Skirt: tapering horizontal wrinkle at the back waistline because the garment is too long at centre back; hip fitting line stays level
Trousers: wrinkle may not form because fabric binds at the crotch; fabric under the buttocks is taut and pulls into wrinkles slanting toward the inseams
Extreme variation: waistband and hip line pulled down across centre back
variations.fabric_requirement: Skirt: shorter centre back body measure needs less length. Trousers: increased buttock profile needs a wider back crotch extension. Extreme variation may need length below the hipline, which also increases the dart created by the slanted centre back seam.
variations.change_required: Shorten the upper centre back area; widen the back crotch extension.

methods.slash: Skirt, fitting garment only: form a parallel tuck near the waistline to remove the excess length; taper to nothing at or near the side seams. Trousers, if the waistband pulls down at centre back: widen the back crotch extension by cutting vertically about 2 inches (5 cm) from the inseam through the back crotch extension to the inseams; turn right side out; lay each set of cut edges over a fabric insert and spread equally at the crotch; taper to nothing at the inseams. For an extreme variation, also cut across the whole back just below the hip fitting line, insert a strip, spread evenly across centre back until the hip line is level, and taper at the side seams.
methods.pivot: Skirt: release the back waist seam; to reduce centre back length, lift the waistline evenly across centre back until smooth; mark the new waistline; blend near side seams; trim; restore dart widths and check lengths. Trousers: widen the back crotch by releasing the crotch seam across the inseams and the inseams from crotch to kneeline; at the crotch let out the back inseam allowances to relieve strain; blend near the kneeline. If a wrinkle forms across centre back, release the back waist and side seams to the hipline; take up centre back at the waist until smooth; let out side seams equally at the back to restore waist circumference; when allowance is minimal, release the waist seam except at centre back; lift the waistline across centre front until smooth; restore dart widths and lengths. Lower the crotch seam by the waist change (see 1 Long Lower Torso).

variations.name: Pelvis tilts toward back
variations.figure_analysis: The pelvic cradle does not lie plumb. As the top tilts backward, the coccyx rotates toward the central axis and the pubic bone moves farther away. Buttocks protrude less than average.
fitting_analysis: Skirt hem hangs against the back of the legs; side seams slant forward at the hem; diagonal wrinkles sag from the side seams toward centre back
Trousers: fabric sags diagonally under the curve of the buttocks and at back creaselines; front may bind at the crotch; hip fitting line and hemline drop at back and rise at front
variations.fabric_requirement: Less fabric length and width at centre back. For an extreme variation, the longer front surface may need more garment length across centre front. Adjustments relax and smooth the fabric; side seams hang plumb; hip fitting line becomes level.
variations.change_required: Shorten the upper centre back area; lengthen the upper centre front area if necessary.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Across the upper centre back, form a parallel tuck to remove the excess fabric length; adjust the tuck width until the hip fitting line is level; taper to nothing at the side seams or near the front darts. Trousers: if horizontal wrinkles form under the buttocks, also deepen the back crotch curve (see 17 Drooped Buttocks).
methods.pivot: Release the back waist seam and the side seams to the hipline. To reduce centre back length, raise the waistline evenly across centre back until the hip fitting line is level; blend into the original stitching near the side seams; narrow the dart widths if needed and check lengths. To restore waist circumference, take up back side seams equally at the waistline; trim. Trousers: deepen the back crotch curve (see 17 Drooped Buttocks).

variations.name: Prominent upper hip curve
variations.figure_analysis: The upper tips of the pelvic cradle flare wider than average, so the sides of the torso curve out abruptly below the waist. The upper hip may be wider than at the hip joints.
fitting_analysis: Fabric along the side seams taut over the upper hip
Skirt: horizontal wrinkles across the side seams just below the waistline; hip fitting line bows upward at the sides
Trousers: diagonal wrinkles from the upper hip to the crotch; hemline rises at the sides
variations.fabric_requirement: More width and length at the upper side seams, because the most prominent curvature is near the waistline. The larger area relaxes the fabric over the hips; the hip fitting line becomes level.
variations.change_required: Widen the upper hip area at the side seams; lengthen the side seams at the waistline if necessary.

methods.slash: Only the curvature and length of the side seamlines change. Cutting the interior causes unnecessary trueing of curved edges; follow the pivot method.
methods.pivot: Release the waistline seam across each side seam area; release the side seams above the hipline. To increase width, let out side seam allowances equally on back and front until the fabric relaxes across the hip curve. To increase length, let out the waistline seam allowance above the side seams until the hip fitting line is level; blend near the darts. This variation may be easier to accommodate by buying the next larger pattern and garment, or by reducing the waistline at the side seams.

variations.name: Sloping upper hip curve
variations.figure_analysis: The upper tips of the pelvic cradle flare less than average, so this part of the hip structure is narrower than at the hip joints. The sides of the torso slope toward the waist instead of curving.
fitting_analysis: Fabric loose along the side seams near the upper hip
Hip fitting line not affected
variations.fabric_requirement: Less fabric width and length at the upper side seams. The only curvature along the side contour occurs at the hipline.
variations.change_required: Narrow the upper hip area at the side seams; shorten the side seams at the waistline if necessary.

methods.slash: Pin a tuck along each side seam where the looseness is greatest to flatten the side seam curvature; taper the tuck to nothing toward the waist and hip lines. If a decrease in length is also needed, form a horizontal tuck near the waistline across each side seam to lift the fabric until it lies smooth; taper to nothing near the darts at back and front.
methods.pivot: Release the side seams above the hipline. To flatten the side seam curve, take in the curved area of the side seam equally on back and front until the fabric is smooth. If a decrease in length is needed, release the waistline seam across the side seams and lift the garment until the fabric is smooth. Blend near the darts at back and front; trim the widened seam allowances.

variations.name: Broad hips
variations.figure_analysis: The bone structures forming the pelvic cradle and the hip joints are larger and wider than average. Soft tissue may lack tone or be more developed. Hip circumference is larger than average.
fitting_analysis: Fabric pulls taut around the fullest part of the hips
In motion a skirt rises gradually; a horizontal fold forms around the waist; hip fitting line and hemline stay level
Trousers: fabric cannot rise at centre front and centre back because it binds at the crotch
Skirts and trousers bought by hip size are too large at the waist (see 4 Small Waist)
variations.fabric_requirement: More fabric width and length at the fullest hip level, so the side seams are longer and noticeably curved near the hipline. The larger garment area lets the fabric relax and lower to the correct position.
variations.change_required: Widen the side seam areas at the hipline.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Determine the fabric needed: subtract the total body hip measurement plus ease from the garment measurement and divide by four (four side seam areas). Release the waist seam across the side seam areas. On back and front near each side seam, cut through the waist seam allowance downward to the hem (skirt) or to the kneeline (trousers), following the lengthwise grain; insert fabric strips. To increase width, spread the cut edges evenly along the slash (on trousers, from waist to crotchline), tapering to nothing at the kneeline. At the waistline take in the side seam areas equally to restore waist circumference; taper to nothing at the hip.
methods.pivot: Determine the amount as above. Skirt: restitch a new side seam to release the calculated amount evenly from the hem edge to the hipline, and blend gradually back to the original seamline at the waistline. Trousers: mark a new side seam across the hipline area to release the width, curve back to the original near the waistline and below the thighline; for a wider leg, continue the new line parallel to the original to the hem. Six-gore skirt: let out the centre panel edges by one quarter of the adjustment and the side seams by three quarters.

variations.name: Narrow hips
variations.figure_analysis: The bone structures forming the pelvic cradle and the hip joints are smaller and narrower than average. There may be less soft tissue, or more taut muscle. Hip circumference is smaller than average.
fitting_analysis: Fabric along the side seams loose at the fullest part of the hips
Hip fitting line and hemline unaffected
Skirts and trousers bought by hip size are too small at the waist (see 3 Large Waist)
variations.fabric_requirement: Less fabric width at the fullest hip level, so the side seams are shorter and less curved than usual at the hipline. The smaller garment area smooths the fabric against the body.
variations.change_required: Narrow the side seam areas at the hipline.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Determine the excess fabric: subtract the total body hip measurement plus ease from the garment measurement and divide by four (four side seam areas). Release the waistline seam across the side seam areas. On back and front near each side seam, form a parallel tuck from the waist seam allowance down to the hem, following the lengthwise grain. On skirts, continue the tuck through the hem edge; on trousers, continue it evenly to the crotchline, then taper to nothing at the kneeline. Let out the side seams equally at the waistline to restore waist circumference; blend near the hipline.
methods.pivot: Determine the amount as above. Skirt: restitch a new side seam taking in the calculated amount evenly from the hem edge to the hipline, blend gradually back to the original seamline at the waistline, and trim. Trousers: mark a new side seam across the hipline area to take in the excess; blend back into the original near the waistline and at the thighline; for a narrower leg, continue the new line parallel to the original to the hem. Six-gore skirt: take in the centre panel edges by one quarter of the adjustment and the side seams by three quarters.

variations.name: Cylindrical-shaped torso (hip area)
variations.figure_analysis: The bone structure forming the pelvic cradle is less oval than average. The torso is narrower from side to side and deeper from centre front through to centre back. Torso circumference does not change.
fitting_analysis: Usually affects the fit only of trousers
Tight diagonal wrinkles pull through the crotch area; more apparent from the back
Fabric may pull into the crotch crevice when the wearer walks, sits or stoops; the strain pulls the waistline and hip fitting line down across centre back
variations.fabric_requirement: Greater body profile depth requires wider crotch extensions. The larger garment area lets the fabric relax and hang smoothly between the legs.
variations.change_required: Widen the back and front crotch extensions.

methods.slash: Place one trouser leg inside the other so the garment is wrong side out; match and pin the inseams together from the crotch to the knee line. About 2 inches (5 cm) from the inseam, cut vertically through the back crotch extension and follow the grain to the inseams. Turn right side out and separate the legs. To increase width, lay each set of cut edges over a fabric insert and spread equally at the crotch to relax the fabric; taper to nothing at the inseams. On the trouser pattern, follow the same process but add one third of the adjustment at the front inseam and two thirds at the back inseam.
methods.pivot: Release the crotch seam across the inseam allowances; release both inseams from crotch to kneeline. To increase width at the crotchline, let out the back inseam by two thirds of the needed amount; let out the new front inseam by one half of the back adjustment. Blend into the original seamline near the kneeline; restitch the crotch seam.

variations.name: Flattened oval-shaped torso (hip area)
variations.figure_analysis: The bone structure forming the pelvic cradle is more oval than average. The torso is wider from side to side and shallower from centre front to centre back.
fitting_analysis: Usually affects the fit only of trousers
Fabric between the legs hangs in loose vertical folds; the excess is an annoyance and restricts walking and stooping
variations.fabric_requirement: Shallower body profile needs narrower crotch extensions. The smaller garment area prevents bagginess between the legs.
variations.change_required: Narrow the back and front crotch extensions.

methods.slash: Release the seam along the back crotch curve. On each trouser leg, form a vertical tuck at the back crotch curve to remove the excess width, following the lengthwise grain and tapering to nothing at the inseam. On the trouser pattern, follow the same process but subtract one third of the adjustment at the front inseam and two thirds at the back inseam.
methods.pivot: Release the crotch seam across the inseam allowances; release both inseams from crotch to kneeline. At the crotch, take in the back inseam area to remove two thirds of the excess fabric; take in the front inseam by one half of the back adjustment. Blend into the original seamline near the kneeline; trim the widened allowances; true the front crotch curve; restitch the crotch seam.

variations.name: High buttocks contour
variations.figure_analysis: Muscle development across the centre back waist area is slight. The muscles forming the buttocks curve are taut and develop higher than average, so the buttocks contour is prominent where shallow and full areas meet abruptly. Distance decreases from the waist straight to the fullest part of the buttocks. When extreme, the depth increases from the fullest buttock to the central axis, so the hip fitting line drops at centre back.
fitting_analysis: Skirts and trousers: fabric near the dart tips, or below the yoke, forms a loose horizontal fold across centre back; hip fitting line stays level
Extreme: trousers bind at the crotch and wrinkles slant from the buttocks toward the inseams
variations.fabric_requirement: Shorter upper centre back needs less length above the hipline, so back darts shorten. Extreme variation needs a wider back crotch extension. A well-fitted girdle can minimise adjustment in most clothing.
variations.change_required: Shorten the upper centre back area; widen the back crotch extension if necessary.

methods.slash: On both skirts and trousers, form a parallel tuck across centre back just above the dart tips to remove the excess length; taper to nothing at the side seams. For an extreme variation, widen the back crotch extension: place one trouser leg inside the other wrong side out and match and pin the inseams from crotch to kneeline; about 2 inches (5 cm) from the inseam, cut vertically through the back crotch extension and follow the grain to the inseams; turn right side out and separate the legs; lay each set of cut edges over a fabric insert and spread equally at the crotch to relax the fabric and raise the hip fitting line to level; taper to nothing at the inseams.
methods.pivot: Release the back waistline seam; lift the waistline evenly across centre back to remove the excess length; blend into the original seamline at the side seams; increase the back dart width to restore waist circumference; trim the widened waist seam allowance. For an extreme variation, let out the back crotch extensions: release stitching across the inseams and both inseams from crotch to kneeline; increase the width of the back extensions at the crotch as needed; blend into the original seamline at the knee.

variations.name: Drooped buttocks
variations.figure_analysis: The buttocks contour is less prominent than average because the muscles and connective tissue lose their tone and the flaccid tissue droops. This increases the crotch length below the hipline.
fitting_analysis: Trousers only
Fabric forms horizontal wrinkles below the buttocks and may pull into the crotch crevice
Waistline and hip fitting line drop across centre back
variations.fabric_requirement: Lowered buttock contour needs a deeper back crotch curve, and a less curved front crotch seam so that a peak does not form at the inseam. The deeper back curve lets the fabric rise and lie smoothly under the buttocks.
variations.change_required: Deepen the curve on the back crotch seamline; flatten the curve on the front crotch seamline.

methods.slash: Pin a horizontal tuck at the wrinkled area to indicate the amount of adjustment.
methods.pivot: Place one trouser leg inside the other wrong side out; match and pin the inseams from crotch to kneeline. Along the back crotch seam, mark the midpoint between the hipline and the inseam, and repeat for the front. Below this point on the back curve, mark ½ inch (1.2 cm) into the trouser area. At the midpoint on the front, mark into the seam allowance enough to form a smooth curve. Begin the new seam near the hipline at the back; stitch a smooth curve through the back adjustment mark and the original crotch-inseam intersection; continue through the front adjustment mark and slope back to the original seamline at the hipline. Clip the widened seam allowance. Try on and repeat until the fabric lies smooth under the buttocks; trim. If the back legs tighten across the inside thigh, see 14 Cylindrical-shaped Torso and let out only the back inseam allowance.

variations.name: Large buttocks
variations.figure_analysis: The muscles and soft tissues forming the buttocks are more developed than average and may lack tone. Hip circumference increases; the distance from the fullest buttock to the central axis and to the waist increases.
fitting_analysis: Basic garment pulls taut over the buttocks; fabric cups under the abdomen
Side seams curve toward the back at the hipline; diagonal wrinkles radiate from the buttocks to each side seam
Skirts: hip fitting line and hemline rise and the hem protrudes at centre back
Trousers: waistband and hip fitting line drop across centre back because fabric binds at the crotch
variations.fabric_requirement: Larger tissue needs more fabric length at the upper centre back and more width across the buttocks; back darts become wider and longer. Trousers need a wider back crotch extension for the greater back profile depth. Adjustments relax the fabric; hip line and hemline become level; the waistband aligns with the body waist.
variations.change_required: Widen the back at the hipline; lengthen the upper centre back area; widen the back crotch extensions.

methods.slash: Release the back waistline seam near the side seams. Skirts: cut the back from the edge of the waistline seam allowance downward through the hem edge, following the lengthwise grain; trousers: cut from the waistline to the kneeline. Insert fabric strips. On skirts spread the cut edges evenly along the entire slash to increase width; on trousers spread them from waistline to crotchline, tapering to nothing at the kneeline. Increase back dart widths on both garments to restore waistline circumference. To widen the trouser back crotch extension, cut about 2 inches (5 cm) from the inseam through the back extension as described for high buttocks, and spread the edges at the crotch. To lengthen centre back, cut across the entire back just below the back dart tips, insert a strip, spread between the dart tips until the hip fitting line is level, taper near each side seam, and reposition and lengthen the back darts as needed.
methods.pivot: Skirts: release the back waistline seam and side seams. Trousers: release the side seams and inseams to the kneeline. On either garment, increase width by letting out both back allowances of the side seams evenly at the hipline; let out an even amount from waist to hem on a skirt, or from waist to crotchline on trousers, and blend into the original seamline at the kneeline. Increase back dart widths to restore waistline circumference; lengthen darts if needed. To increase back crotch ease on trousers, release the crotch seam across the inseam allowances, release the inseam from crotch to kneeline, let out the back inseam allowances equally at the crotch to relieve strain, and blend above the knee. To lengthen centre back, let out the waist seam allowance evenly across centre back until the hip fitting line is level, and blend into the original seamline at each side seam.

variations.name: Flat buttocks
variations.figure_analysis: The muscles and soft tissues forming the buttocks are less developed than average. This decreases the hip circumference. The distance decreases from the fullest part of the buttocks to the central axis and to the waist.
fitting_analysis: Garment loose across the buttocks; loose diagonal wrinkles droop from the upper side seam areas toward the buttocks
Hip fitting line drops across centre back
Trousers: loose diagonal wrinkles droop from the side seams and inseams toward the creaselines on each leg
variations.fabric_requirement: Less fabric length at the upper centre back and less width across the buttocks; back darts narrower and shorter. A more shallow back profile needs a narrower back crotch extension. Adjustments smooth the fabric and bring the hip fitting line level.
variations.change_required: Narrow the back at the hipline; shorten the upper centre back area; narrow the back crotch extensions.

methods.slash: Release the back waistline seam near the side seams. To remove the excess fabric on the back, form a parallel vertical tuck from the waistline toward the hem, following the lengthwise grain. End at the hem on skirts; on trousers begin at the crotchline and taper to nothing at the kneeline. Decrease dart widths to restore waistline circumference and shorten darts as needed for the smaller curvature. To narrow the trouser back crotch extension, release the stitching along the back crotch curve, form a vertical tuck at the crotch on each leg to remove the excess width following the lengthwise grain, and taper to nothing at the inseam. To shorten centre back, form a horizontal parallel tuck across the garment between the back dart tips to lift the hip fitting line to level; taper to nothing at the side seams.
methods.pivot: Release the back waist seam and back waist darts. Skirts: release the side seams. Trousers: release side seams to the kneeline. To narrow, take in the back side seam evenly from waist to hem on a skirt, or from waist to crotchline on trousers; taper the trouser side seam into the original seamline at the kneeline. Decrease dart length and width for the smaller curvature. To reduce back crotch looseness on trousers, release the crotch seam across the inseam allowances, release the inseam from crotch to kneeline, take in the back inseam area equally at the crotch, and taper into the original seamline above the kneeline. To shorten centre back, lift the waistline evenly across centre back until the hip fitting line is level; blend into the original seamline at each side seam.

variations.name: Prominent pubic area
variations.figure_analysis: The pubic bone or flesh may be more forward, lower or larger than average. This creates a more abruptly curved contour at the front crotch, and the front surface of the torso is vertical rather than slightly sloped.
fitting_analysis: Trousers only
Wrinkles follow the front crotch curve, or fabric pulls into the crotch crevice because the front crotch curve is too shallow
Extreme variation: vertical fitting lines pull toward each other at the front crotchline
variations.fabric_requirement: A more prominent bone structure needs a more abrupt curve at the front crotch seamline. Extreme variation may need a wider front crotch extension, which increases the crotch length from hipline to inseam.
variations.change_required: Deepen the curve on the front crotch.

methods.slash: Only the angle and curvature of the centre front and the crotch seamline change. Cutting the interior causes unnecessary trueing of sloped and curved edges; follow the pivot method.
methods.pivot: Place one trouser leg inside the other wrong side out. Flatten the centre front area of the trousers and align the fabric grain. To relieve the strain at the crotch contour, draw a new, more rounded front crotch seamline beginning at the original centre front/hipline intersection. Blend into the original crotch seamline at the inseam. The back crotch curve may need flattening slightly to prevent a peak at the inseam. Trim the widened seam allowance after stitching.

variations.name: Recessed pubic area
variations.figure_analysis: The pubic bone or flesh may be smaller, or the area may set back more deeply than average. This creates a crotch with a more sloping contour rather than a curved one, and the front surface of the torso slopes noticeably.
fitting_analysis: Trousers only
Taut horizontal wrinkles pull across the seam at the front crotch area
Vertical grainlines pull toward each other at the groin
variations.fabric_requirement: A less prominent bone structure needs a flatter curve in the front crotch seamline.
variations.change_required: Flatten the curve on the front crotch seamline.

methods.slash: Only the angle and curvature of the centre front and the crotch seamline change. Cutting the interior causes unnecessary trueing of sloped and curved edges; follow the pivot method.
methods.pivot: Release the lower half of the front crotch seam and put the trousers on. Along the crotch curve, mark where the greatest increase is needed. Remove the trousers, place one leg inside the other wrong side out, and flatten the front area, aligning the grain. To bring the stitching line closer to the body surface, draw a new, less curved front crotch seamline beginning at the centre front/hipline intersection, continue through the adjustment mark, and blend into the original crotch seamline at the inseam. Deepen the back crotch curve slightly to prevent a peak at the inseam.

variations.name: Long legs
variations.figure_analysis: The leg bones are longer than average. The additional length may occur above or below the knee, or be distributed equally.
fitting_analysis: Hem position is too high on the leg for pleasing proportions
Closely fitted garments that flare near the knee: the flare origin may be too far above the knee
Long tapered trousers: hem circumference may look too small because it pulls taut against the leg
Hip fitting line remains level
variations.fabric_requirement: Additional leg length needs longer fabric below the thighline. For closely fitted garments that flare or taper near the knee, the extra length may go above or below the kneeline or be distributed equally. Ruffles, kick pleats and similar details may need more length in the garment area, in the detail, or both.
variations.change_required: Lengthen skirt and trousers evenly below the thighline.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Cut around the entire skirt or both trouser legs below the thighline or above the design detail. Insert fabric strips. To increase length, separate the cut edges evenly. Observe the proportions of the body, garment and detail, and adjust each garment area to enhance the garment and wearer.
methods.pivot: Release the hem and press it flat; mark the new hemline. If the resulting hem width is too narrow for the style, fabric or wearer, face the hem edge: narrow hems look skimpy and remodelled. Trousers may taper ½ inch (1.2 cm) higher at the front crease to prevent excess break above the instep; trim the hem to an even width after tapering. For closely fitted garments that begin to flare, mark the place on the side and inseams where the flare begins; stitch new seams from the original seamlines at the hem to the adjustment marks near the kneeline; blend into the original seamline in a slight curve. Skirt length may also be added by restyling with a yoke: lower the waistline and add a yoke wide enough to correct the total length. To adjust garment width at the yokeline, narrow and shorten the darts, convert them to ease, or eliminate them; adjust side seam allowances as necessary.

variations.name: Short legs
variations.figure_analysis: The leg bones are shorter than average. The shorter length may occur above or below the knee, or be distributed equally.
fitting_analysis: Hem position is too low on the leg for pleasing proportions
Trouser hems that touch the floor fray quickly, hide the feet and are dangerous
Closely fitted garments that flare near the knee: the flare origin may be too far below the knee for walking comfort or proportion
Hip fitting line remains level
variations.fabric_requirement: Decreased leg length needs shorter fabric below the thighline. For closely fitted garments that flare near the knee, the length may need reducing above or below the kneeline or distributed equally. Ruffles, kick pleats and similar details may need less length in the garment area, the detail, or both.
variations.change_required: Shorten the skirt or trousers evenly below the thighline.

methods.slash: Form a parallel tuck around the garment below the thighline or above the design detail, to adjust for the total appropriate length. Observe the proportions of the body, garment and detail for a fashion garment, and adjust each garment area to enhance the garment and wearer.
methods.pivot: Release the hem and press it flat; mark the new hemline. Check the resulting hem width and remove the excess: hems that are too wide for the fabric, style or wearer look bulky and heavy. Trousers may taper upward ½ inch (1.2 cm) at the front crease to prevent excess break above the instep; trim the hem to an even width after tapering. For closely fitted garments that begin to flare or taper above the knee, mark the place on the side and inseams where the flare begins, for both fit and walking comfort; stitch new seams from the original seamlines at the new hemline to the adjustment marks near the kneeline; blend into the original seamline in a slight curve. If a style detail is at the skirt hem, reduce length at the waistline instead: release the waist seam and lift the garment evenly until the hem position is correct; restore waist circumference by forming new darts, widening and lengthening the original darts, or converting the extra width to gathers or tucks; adjust side seams to remove excess fullness.

variations.name: Large thighs at inside
variations.figure_analysis: The muscles and soft tissues forming the inner thigh contour are more developed than average. The inner surfaces of the legs may touch when the wearer stands, and rub together as the person walks.
fitting_analysis: Trousers only
Fabric taut across the upper inseam and may rise to form tight horizontal wrinkles below the crotch
When walking, the fabric on the back leg pulls forward between the legs
variations.fabric_requirement: Fuller thighs need a wider front crotch extension and a straighter front inseam from crotch to knee. Excessive wear occurs on the fabric at the inseam area; stable, closely woven fabrics are more durable and comfortable. Use a shorter stitch or double stitching on the crotch and upper inseams.
variations.change_required: Widen the front crotch extensions.

methods.slash: Place one trouser leg inside the other wrong side out; match and pin the inseams from crotch to kneeline. About 1 inch (2.5 cm) from the inseam, cut vertically through the front extension and follow the lengthwise grain to the inseams. Turn right side out and separate the legs. Lay each slashed area over a fabric insert; spread equally at the crotch as needed to relax the fabric; taper to nothing at the knee. If the seamline along the upper inseam forms a curve, draw a new, straighter inseam seamline beginning at the crotch/inseam intersection and tapering to nothing at the knee.
methods.pivot: Release the crotch seamline across the inseam allowances; release the inseams from crotch to kneeline. To increase width at the crotch, let out the front inseam allowances equally to relieve the strain. Form the new inseam seamline as a rather straight line. Blend into the original seamline above the kneeline. Check for fit and comfort; repeat for the back crotch extension if necessary.

variations.name: Shallow thighs at inside
variations.figure_analysis: The muscles and soft tissues forming the inner thigh contour are less developed than average. When the person stands, there is a definite, visible space between the legs from the crotch nearly to the knee.
fitting_analysis: Trousers only
Fabric loose along the upper inseam and hangs in loose vertical folds
variations.fabric_requirement: A flatter inner thigh needs a narrower front crotch extension, which produces a more vertical inseam.
variations.change_required: Narrow the front crotch extensions.

methods.slash: Release the seam along the front crotch curve. To remove the excess fabric width, form a vertical tuck on each crotch extension about 1 inch (2.5 cm) from the inseam. Follow the lengthwise grain, tapering the tuck to nothing at the inseams just above the knee.
methods.pivot: Release the crotch seamline across the inseam allowances; release the inseams from crotch to kneeline. To remove the excess fabric at the crotch, take up the front inseam areas equally as needed. Blend into the original centre front at the hipline. Form a new inseam seamline as a rather straight line; blend into the original seamline near the kneeline.

variations.name: Large thighs at front
variations.figure_analysis: The thigh muscles across the front of the legs are fuller than average. This creates the illusion that the groin recess is deeper than average.
fitting_analysis: Fabric pulls taut across the front of the upper thighs and cups under the buttocks
Side seams curve toward the front
Skirts: when the wearer walks, the front fabric rises to form a horizontal fold at the groin, and the hemline rises across centre front
Trousers: horizontal folds form across each inseam near the crotch, may cause the front creaselines to curve toward each other at the thigh, and hang toward each other at the hem
variations.fabric_requirement: Thigh fullness needs more fabric width at the midfront areas. On a skirt, transfer the front dart to the hem edge to place the flare over the thigh; the wider garment area relaxes and hangs smoothly below the hipline. A-line, circular and gathered skirts already include more fullness at thigh level and may need no alteration. On trousers the dart transfer also widens the area from the front creaseline to the crotch extension.
variations.change_required: Widen the midfront areas.

methods.slash: Skirts: slash halfway between each side seam and centre front, from hem to waistline, following the lengthwise grain. Insert fabric strips. To increase width, spread the cut edges evenly from the hem to the thighline. Taper to nothing at the dart tip area or at the waistline as the body requires. Trousers: place one leg inside the other wrong side out, match and pin the inseams from crotch to kneeline, and about 1 inch (2.5 cm) from the inseam cut through the front extension as for large thighs at inside .
methods.pivot: Skirts: release side seams from hip to hem; mark new side seams parallel to the originals from hem to thigh. To transfer the waist dart to the hem, release the remaining side seam and the waistline to the dart; decrease the side waist dart by half its width (one third if only one dart); lengthen the side seam at the waistline by about half the width change at the thigh; taper back to the original seam at the dart. To restore side length, shorten the new side seam at the hem by the amount it was raised at the waist; pin side seams together up to thigh level, put on the skirt, taper the side seam to the waist, and mark the new front hemline. Trousers: release the side seam from hip to kneeline, the waistline, centre front and the front crotch seam across the inseam allowances; release the inseam from crotch to kneeline; let out front seam allowances of side and inseam as needed so the creases and side seams hang plumb. The longer crotch extension may sag against the groin: raise the waist across centre front to remove the excess, mark a parallel new waistline, taper to the original at the side seam, and flatten the front crotch curve slightly. On the pattern, obtain the midfront width increase by transferring the dart to the centre and inseam.

variations.name: Large thighs at sides
variations.figure_analysis: The muscles and soft tissues across the sides of the legs extend more than average and may lack tone. The greatest width and side curvature are below the hipline.
fitting_analysis: Fabric pulls taut across the side seams at the thighline and cups under the buttocks
When walking, the garment rises and forms a horizontal wrinkle above each thigh; hip fitting line rises at the sides
Trousers: fabric pulls taut across the upper inseam; front creaselines curve outward at thigh level and slant away from each other at the hems
variations.fabric_requirement: Fullness at the sides of the legs needs more fabric width below the hipline. The greatest curvature along the side seam is at thigh level, because the dart concealed in the side seam widens. The wider area relaxes over the thigh and the hip fitting line becomes level. A-line, circular and gathered skirts include more fullness at thigh level and may need no alteration.
variations.change_required: Widen the side seam areas at the thighline.

methods.slash: Adjust both the front and back of a skirt to keep the two widths balanced. Release the waist seam across the side seam areas. On back and front near each side seam, cut from the edges of the waist seam allowance through the hem edge, following the lengthwise grain. Insert fabric strips and spread each set of cut edges evenly along the entire slash to gain the needed width. Take in the side seams equally at the waist to restore waist circumference; taper to nothing just below the hipline.
methods.pivot: Skirts: release side seams from the hem past the hipline where tightness begins. At the thighline let out the back and front seam allowances equally until the fabric relaxes; continue the adjustment an even amount through the hem edge; blend into the original seamline above the hipline. Trousers: release side seams from hip to kneeline; let out back and front seam allowances equally at the thighline; blend into the original seamline near the ends of the opened areas.

variations.name: Outward knee rotation
variations.figure_analysis: The legs bow outward, with the greatest curvature at the knee. The toes often point inward to counterbalance the body.
fitting_analysis: Trousers: front creaselines bow outward at the knees and slant inward at the hems
At the kneeline the fabric is taut along the side seams and loose at the inseams; diagonal wrinkles form across the inseam at the kneeline
Hemline rises at the sides
variations.fabric_requirement: Outward curvature of the legs needs more length at the side seams and less at the inseams. The adjusted seam lengths reposition the fabric to relax and lie smoothly. The hemline becomes level. Flared skirts and trousers help camouflage the variation and may need no adjustment.
variations.change_required: Lengthen the side seams; shorten the inseams.

methods.slash: Near the thighline, cut across both side seams. Continue cutting along the crosswise grain to the front and back creases. Insert fabric strips. To increase side seam length, spread each set of edges equally at the side seams until the fabric relaxes and the front creaselines straighten below the knee. To shorten the inseams, continue following the crosswise grain with a tuck across each inseam to remove an amount equal to the side adjustment; taper each adjustment to nothing at the creases. For a slight variation, decrease the inseam length by forming a tuck across each inseam at thigh level; adjust the tuck widths equally until the front creaselines hang plumb; taper each tuck to nothing at the side seams. On the pattern, establish a new grainline parallel to the original creaselines below the knee.
methods.pivot: Release the entire waistline; the centre front and back areas require lifting. Clip the crotch seam allowance at ½ inch (1.2 cm) intervals across the inseam area. Put on the trousers; lift the waistline across centre front and back and lower it at the sides until the legs hang smoothly and the front creaselines straighten below the knee. Blend near the sides; clip at the crotch to relieve tightness; stitch the new crotch seamline the book gives as ¼ inch (0.6 mm) below the ends of the clips (likely a typo for 6 mm; confirm before use); taper into the original seamline near the hipline; trim the widened crotch seam allowance. For a slight variation, release the back and front waistline across the side seam areas nearly to the centres, lower the waist at the sides to relieve the strain at the knee, and taper into the original waist seamline near centre front and back.

variations.name: Inward knee rotation
variations.figure_analysis: The legs bow inward, with the greatest curvature at the knee. The toes often point outward to counterbalance the body.
fitting_analysis: Trousers only
Front creaselines bow inward at the knees and slant outward at the hems
At the kneeline the fabric is taut along the inseams and loose at the sides; diagonal wrinkles form from the inner edge of each knee upward toward each creaseline
Hemline rises at the inseams; on tight-legged trousers a loose horizontal fold forms across each side seam at the kneeline
variations.fabric_requirement: Inward curvature needs more length at the inseams and less at the side seams. The adjusted seam lengths reposition the fabric to relax and lie smoothly. The hemline becomes level. Trousers that flare gently from thigh to hem camouflage the variation.
variations.change_required: Shorten the side seams; lengthen the inseams.

methods.slash: To decrease side seam length, form a tuck across each side seam at thigh level. Adjust the tuck widths equally until the front creaselines hang plumb; taper each tuck to nothing at the inseams. If tightness is present along the inseams at the knee area, release the stitching from the thighline to below the kneeline; let out the seam allowance equally at the knee until the fabric relaxes; taper into the original seamline near the crotch and hemline. Check the hemline position and adjust evenly. On the pattern, establish a new grainline parallel to the original creaselines below the knee.
methods.pivot: Release the entire waistline except a short distance across centre front and centre back. Lift the waist at the side seams until the trouser legs hang smoothly and the front creaselines are plumb below the knee. Blend into the original seamline near centre front and centre back.

variations.name: Hyperextended calves
variations.figure_analysis: The lower leg bones appear to bow toward the back. The back curvature may result from tense, locked knees, and back muscle development may be involved.
fitting_analysis: Trousers: fabric forms a loose horizontal fold above the calves
Side seams may curve toward the back at calf level; hip fitting line level; hemline rises slightly across the back
variations.fabric_requirement: Decreasing the length of fabric across the upper centre back lifts the fabric so it hangs vertically from the buttocks curvature. The variation may need a deeper back crotch curve. Trouser styles with fuller legs camouflage the variation and may need no adjustment.
variations.change_required: Shorten the upper centre back area; restore back crotch length by lowering the crotch curve.

methods.slash: Below the crotchline, form a tuck across the creaseline to lift the fabric until it hangs smoothly and away from the surface of the calves. Taper to nothing at the side seams and inseams.
methods.pivot: Release the back waist seam. Before the centre back can be lifted, clip the crotch seam allowance every ½ inch (1.2 cm) along the back crotch curve. Put on the trousers and lift the waistline across centre back by a parallel amount until the fabric hangs smoothly and away from the calves. Blend into the original seamline at the side seams. Continue the clips deep enough to relieve the strain at the crotch. Stitch a new crotch seam the book gives as ¼ inch (0.6 mm) below the ends of the clips (likely a typo for 6 mm; confirm before use). Blend into the original seamline at back and front near the hipline.

variations.name: Large legs
variations.figure_analysis: The leg bones may be larger than average. The muscles and other soft tissues are more developed and may lack tone. The larger development may occur along the entire leg or only over the upper or lower portion. Excess soft tissue may fill the ankle and conceal the angularity of the bone structure there.
fitting_analysis: Trousers primarily: fabric pulls taut around each leg and forms horizontal wrinkles at the crotchline
Hemlines rise; upper part of the trousers looks loose and bloused
Skirts: refer to 12 Broad Hips and 27 Large Thighs at Sides; a slightly flared skirt with the hemline just above the fullest part of the calves camouflages the fullness
variations.fabric_requirement: Larger leg circumference needs more fabric width below the hipline on the back and front of the trousers. Larger trouser legs let the upper trouser area lower to the correct position, and the bloused appearance disappears. The larger leg areas relax over the figure and hang free. Purchasing a larger size makes adjustment simpler; reduce the waistline instead (see 4 Small Waist).
variations.change_required: Widen the back and front trouser legs.

methods.slash: Near the midfront and midback of each trouser leg, cut along the lengthwise grain from the hem through the hipline. Insert fabric strips. From the hemline to the kneeline, spread the cut edges evenly to relax the fabric and restore the ease; taper to nothing at the hipline. On the pattern, one fourth of the increase should be added at each.
methods.pivot: Release the crotch seam across the inseam allowances; release the inseams from crotch to kneeline; release the side seams from hem to hipline. From hemline to kneeline let out front and back side seam allowances evenly until the fabric relaxes and the ease is restored; blend the side seam adjustments into the original seamline at the hipline. Let out the inseam evenly to the knee and taper to the crotch, decreasing to one half the amount at the crotchline. Pattern note: add one fourth of the increase at each side seam and inseam to keep the trouser leg balanced.

variations.name: Thin legs
variations.figure_analysis: The leg bones may be smaller than average. The muscles and other soft tissues are firmer or less developed than average. The smaller development may occur along the entire leg or only over the upper or lower portion. The angularity of the ankle bone is usually quite apparent.
fitting_analysis: Trousers primarily: the whole trouser leg area is loose and appears too large; fabric hangs in slight vertical folds
Looseness begins at the hipline but is most apparent from crotch to kneeline
Closely fitted trousers and straight or extremely full skirts emphasise the thinness of the lower leg
variations.fabric_requirement: Smaller leg circumference needs less fabric width below the hipline on back and front of the trousers. Narrower leg areas lie closer to the leg and improve the proportion between garment and wearer.
variations.change_required: Narrow the back and front trouser legs.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Along each creaseline of both trouser legs, form a parallel tuck from the hem to the crotchline. Adjust the tuck widths as needed to remove the excess fabric; taper to nothing at the hipline. On the pattern, remove one fourth of the total decrease at each side seam and inseam to keep the legs balanced.
methods.pivot: Release the crotch seam across the inseam allowances; release the inseams from crotch to kneeline. Along both side seams and inseams, take in the back and front trouser area evenly from hem to kneeline to remove the excess fabric. Blend the side seam adjustments into the original seamline at the hipline. Keep the inseam adjustment even to the knee, then taper to the crotchline. Remove the original stitching on the adjusted areas of the side seams and the remainder of the inseam.

variations.name: High neck base at sides
variations.figure_analysis: There is less than average angularity where the neck edges meet the shoulders. The heavier muscles and body tissues that fill this area create an illusion of sloping shoulders.
fitting_analysis: Front neckline uncomfortably tight; diagonal wrinkles pull from the neckline toward the armscyes
A loose horizontal fold may form across the base of the neck
Back neckline may rise at centre back; strain makes the armscye edges ripple and look too large
Chest and blade fitting lines rise at body centres; a centre-front opening will not close properly at the neckline
variations.fabric_requirement: Neck fullness needs longer front neckline extensions and more length at upper centre back. Back and front necklines should be widened. The larger garment area relieves tightness at the front neck and lets the back neckline and armscyes relax and align with the body; chest and blade lines become level.
variations.change_required: Lengthen the front neckline extensions and the upper centre back area; increase the neckline width.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Garment front: slash through the neck seam allowance near each shoulder seam, continuing across to each armscye seamline. Insert fabric strips and spread each set of cut edges equally at the neckline until the fabric relaxes. Garment back: slash across the upper blade area from shoulder tip to shoulder tip; insert a fabric strip; spread the cut edges evenly below the neckline until the tightness is relieved and both fitting lines are level; taper the adjustments to nothing at the armscyes; widen the neckline opening at the shoulder area as needed.
methods.pivot: Release the shoulder seams. At the neckline, let out the front and back seam allowances equally to relieve tightness and straighten the chest and blade fitting lines; taper to nothing at the armscyes. Across centre back, raise the neckline seam by the amount of the change at the shoulders; blend into the original at the new shoulder seamline; widen the neckline opening at the shoulder area as needed.

variations.name: Shallow neck base at sides
variations.figure_analysis: A definite angle is defined where the neck edges meet the shoulders. The shallowness, caused by lighter than average muscle development and smaller deposits of soft tissue, creates an illusion of square shoulders.
fitting_analysis: Neckline loose at the shoulder area and may appear too low at centre front
A loose horizontal fold may sag across centre front and centre back near the neckline
Chest and blade fitting lines remain level
variations.fabric_requirement: Shallow neck areas need shorter front neckline extensions and less length at upper centre back. Back and front neckline width may require adjustment. The smaller garment areas lie smoothly against the neck base at the back and front.
variations.change_required: Shorten the front neckline extensions and the upper centre back area; decrease the neckline width.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Garment front: form a tuck through the neck seam allowance near each shoulder seam. Keep the shoulderline in the correct position. Adjust the tuck widths until the excess fabric is removed at the neckline; taper to nothing at each armscye. Below the back neckline, form a parallel tuck across the centre back area; adjust its width until the fabric lies smoothly against the body; taper to nothing at each armscye. Narrow the neckline opening at the shoulderline as needed.
methods.pivot: Release the shoulder seams. At the neckline take up the back and front seam allowances equally to remove the excess fabric; taper to nothing at the armscyes. Across centre back, lower the neckline seam by the amount of the change at the shoulders; blend into the original at the new shoulder seamline. Narrow the neckline opening at the shoulderline as needed.

variations.name: Large neck
variations.figure_analysis: The neck circumference is larger than average, because the neck muscles are heavier and the neckbones and concentration of other soft tissues may be larger. The muscles and soft tissues may also lack tone.
fitting_analysis: When the closure is forced shut, the back neckline rises; the front neckline tightens uncomfortably and a circular wrinkle forms below it
Front armscye edges may ripple and look too large; lower armscye areas on the front pull against the arm hinges and cause discomfort
Chest and blade fitting lines rise at the body centres
variations.fabric_requirement: A larger neck circumference needs a neckline opening that is wider at the sides and lower at centre front. The larger opening relieves the tightness so the fabric lies smoothly against the neck; chest and blade fitting lines become level.
variations.change_required: Widen the back and front neckline; lower the front neckline.

methods.slash: Fitting garment only. Garment front: clip through the neckline seam allowance at ½ inch (1.2 cm) intervals across the centre front area; extend the cuts into the bodice area deep enough to relieve the tightness; continue clipping to the same depth around the entire front neckline. Clip the back neckline seam allowance as needed near each shoulder seam. Draw the new neck seamline along the line formed by the ends of the clips; blend the new line into the original near centre back. If only the front is tight, see 37 Forward Neck.
methods.pivot: Proceed as stated in the slash method.

variations.name: Thin neck
variations.figure_analysis: The neck circumference is smaller than average because the neck muscles are lighter, and the neck bones and concentration of other soft tissues may be smaller.
fitting_analysis: The garment neckline area is smooth but does not reach the base of the neck at the sides or at centre front
Poor proportion between the larger neckline opening and the smallness of the neck
Chest and blade fitting lines remain level
variations.fabric_requirement: A smaller neck circumference needs a neckline opening that is narrower at the sides and higher at centre front. The smaller opening aligns with the base of the neck and improves the proportion between opening and neck.
variations.change_required: Narrow the back and front neckline; raise the neckline as needed at the body contours.

methods.slash: Leave the neckline seam allowance extended toward the neck, or lay the front neckline over a fabric insert. Align the grain of both fabrics. Across centre front, raise the seamline by the desired amount. Continue marking the new neckline along the base of the neck. At the shoulderline, begin to blend the new line into the original near centre back.
methods.pivot: Proceed as stated in the slash method.

variations.name: Forward neck
variations.figure_analysis: The head may tilt forward more than average and rest in front of the central axis of the body. The forward thrust of the head sharpens the angle where the neck meets the chest. This increases front neck depth and lengthens the upper centre back area. Front neck depth also increases from prominent neck tendons or excess soft tissue.
fitting_analysis: With a basic jewel neckline, strain tightens the front neckline and forms a fold of fabric below it
Shoulder lines pull forward at the edges of the neck
Back neckline tightens or may rise; blade fitting line rises across centre back; chest fitting line remains level
A neckline worn open or designed lower at centre front does not require alteration
variations.fabric_requirement: The fuller front neck area needs a deeper front neckline. The length adjustments relieve the strain and let the fabric lie smoothly below the neckline, so it can align with the neck base; the blade fitting line becomes level.
variations.change_required: Lower the front neckline.

methods.slash: Garment front: clip through the neckline seam allowance at ½ inch (1.2 cm) intervals across the centre front area. Extend the cuts into the bodice area deep enough to relieve tightness and to let the shoulder seam align with the shoulder. Continue with shorter clips toward the shoulderline as needed. Draw the new front neck seamline along the line formed by the ends of the clips; blend into the original seamline near the shoulder.
methods.pivot: Proceed as for the slash method.

variations.name: Dowager hump
variations.figure_analysis: An enlargement of the bone structure and other tissues develops high on the spine. The width and length of the upper centre back area increase. This creates the illusion of rounded shoulders and is usually accompanied by a forward head position and/or a hollow chest.
fitting_analysis: The garment pulls taut across the back of the neck
Back armscye edges ripple and appear too large
The strain tightens the front neckline and causes a fold of fabric below it
Blade fitting line and back waistline rise at the body centres
variations.fabric_requirement: Fullness over the spine needs more fabric length and width at the upper centre back. Neck darts are needed to shape the fabric. The longer, more shaped garment area relieves strain and lets back and front lie smoothly; chest and blade fitting lines and waistline become level.
variations.change_required: Lengthen and widen the upper centre back area.

methods.slash: Slash through the back neck seam allowance at both mid-back areas. Cut at a slight diagonal toward the blade fitting line, then continue over to the armscye seamlines. Insert fabric strips from each armscye to the blade line. Spread each set of cut edges evenly until the armscyes align with the body contour and the blade fitting line becomes level. Slash from one shoulder dart tip to the other following the crossgrain; insert a fabric strip; lift the neckline section evenly until the neckline rises to a comfortable and attractive position; taper to nothing at the dart tips. Near the neckline slashes, form darts of equal widths to remove the excess fabric and create the shaping for the body contour.
methods.pivot: Release the back armscye, the shoulder seams and the back shoulder darts. Smooth the fabric over the blade areas until the blade fitting line is level; retain part of the shoulder dart as ease if needed. Lay the front shoulder seamline over the extended back shoulder seam allowances. The original armscye and neckline lines will no longer match, but the two sets should align similarly on each shoulder. Form new neck darts of equal widths to remove excess fabric from the back neckline. Across centre back, draw a new neckline at an attractive, comfortable position; blend smoothly into the front neckline at the shoulder. If the front neckline is too high, follow 37 Forward Neck. If excess fabric length remains at centre front, see 48 Hollow Chest.

variations.name: Broad shoulders
variations.figure_analysis: The collar bones are longer than average. The bone structure of the spine, collar bones and shoulder joints may be heavier also. These factors increase the body width and its circumference at shoulder tip level. The arm structure is not affected.
fitting_analysis: Horizontal wrinkles pull across the armscye seamlines
Sleeve caps pull upward and toward the body centres; sleeve caps appear too tight and both upper and lower sleeve areas appear too short
The ends of the chest and blade fitting lines rise
variations.fabric_requirement: Broad shoulders need longer shoulder seamlines on the garment. The added fabric width at the upper blade and chest areas lets the armscyes align with the body contour and relieves strain on the sleeves; they lower to the correct position on the arm. The fitting lines become level.
variations.change_required: Lengthen the shoulder seamlines.

methods.slash: Release 2 inches (5 cm) of each shoulder seam at the armscye areas. Slash the opened shoulder seam near each armscye and continue diagonally down to the armscye seamline at the arm hinge areas. Insert fabric strips. To increase width, spread the cut edges equally at the shoulder until the armscye seamlines align with the crest of the shoulder curves; taper to nothing at the armscye. True and restitch the shoulder seam using the original slope of the neckline portion as a guide.
methods.pivot: If the sleeves are not attached, mark the new armscye seamlines from shoulder to arm hinge areas and set in the sleeves along them. If attached, release the sleeve caps down to the arm hinge areas at front and back; turn under the sleeve cap seam allowance along the eased seamline; move the sleeve cap outward along the shoulderline until the seamline sits comfortably; pin, then stitch the armscye.

variations.name: Narrow shoulders
variations.figure_analysis: The collar bones are shorter than average. The bone structure of the spine, collar bones and shoulder joints may be lighter also. These factors decrease body width and circumference at shoulder tip level. The arm structure is not affected.
fitting_analysis: Armscye seamlines drop off the crest of the shoulder curves and lie against the arms
Sleeve caps sag and appear too large
Garment fabric loose at the chest edges; front armscye cuts against the arm hinge
Ends of the chest and blade fitting lines droop
variations.fabric_requirement: Narrow shoulders need shorter shoulder seamlines on the garment. The reduced fabric width at the upper blade and chest areas lets the armscyes align with the body contour; sleeves rise to the correct position on the shoulder without adjustment; fitting lines become level.
variations.change_required: Shorten the shoulder seamlines.

methods.slash: Release 2 inches (5 cm) of each shoulder seam at the armscye areas. Pin tucks of equal widths across the opened seam areas near each armscye seam. Adjust the width of the tucks until the armscye seamlines align with the crest of the shoulder curves. True and restitch the shoulder seam using the original slope of the neckline portion as a guide.
methods.pivot: If the sleeves are not attached, mark the new armscye seamlines from shoulder to arm hinge areas, clip widened seam allowances as needed, and set in the sleeves along them. If attached, release the sleeve caps down to the arm hinge areas at front and back; turn under the sleeve cap seam allowance along the eased seamline; move the sleeve inward along the shoulderline until the seamline is comfortable; pin and stitch the armscye.

variations.name: Square shoulders
variations.figure_analysis: The collar bones slope less than average because they meet the vertical bone structure of the spine more nearly at 90-degree angles. The distance increases from the waist up to the base of the arm joints. The arm structure is not affected.
fitting_analysis: Tight diagonal wrinkles run from the upper armscye area to the bust, the blade, and the biceps areas
Sleeves rise and appear too short; ends of the chest and blade fitting lines rise; centres of the cap fitting lines rise
variations.fabric_requirement: The higher shoulder joint position lifts the armscye farther from the waistline. Side seams lengthen and shoulder seams slope less. The raised armscye aligns with the body contour and relieves strain at the neckline; chest and blade fitting lines become level; sleeves fit without adjustment.
variations.change_required: Lengthen each side seam at the armscye to raise the armscye to a higher position.

methods.slash: Remove the sleeves. Slash across the armscye seam allowances about ½ inch (1.2 cm) below the shoulder seams on both back and front; continue over to the neck seamlines. Insert fabric strips. To increase length, spread each set of cut edges equally at the armscye until the fabric lies smooth; taper each slash to nothing at the neckline. Mark the new higher position of the armscye seamline across the underarm seams to restore armscye depth; blend smoothly into the original seamline at front and back; reattach the sleeves using the new armscye seamline markings.
methods.pivot: Remove the sleeves; release the shoulder seams; let out the shoulder seam allowances equally at the armscyes on back and front until the fabric relaxes and the chest and blade fitting lines become level. Raise the lower armscye seamline position to restore armscye depth; blend into the original seamline at the arm hinge area; attach the sleeves using the new armscye seamlines.

variations.name: Sloping shoulders
variations.figure_analysis: The collar bones slope more than average because they meet the vertical bone structure of the spine at wider angles. The distance decreases from the waist up to the base of the arm joints. The arm structure is not affected.
fitting_analysis: Sleeve caps sag off the crest of the shoulder and appear too large
Fabric along the armscyes sags into diagonal wrinkles from the neckline to the lower armscye areas
Ends of the chest and blade fitting lines droop; centres of the cap fitting line also droop
variations.fabric_requirement: The lower shoulder joint position lowers the armscye closer to the waistline. Side seams shorten and shoulder seams slope more. The lowered armscye aligns with the body contour; chest and blade fitting lines become level; sleeves fit without adjustment.
variations.change_required: Shorten each side seam at the armscye to drop the armscye to a lower position and increase the slope of the shoulder.

methods.slash: Remove the sleeves. Clip the lower armscye seam allowance at ½ inch (1.2 cm) intervals to release the tension. Remove the excess armscye length equally with a tuck near the shoulder seams on back and front; taper each tuck to nothing at the neckline. Mark the new lower position of the armscye seamline across the underarm seams to restore armscye depth; blend smoothly into the original seamline at front and back; reattach the sleeves using the new armscye seamlines.
methods.pivot: Remove the sleeves. Clip the lower armscye seam allowances at ½ inch (1.2 cm) intervals to release tension. Take in both back and front shoulder seam areas equally at the armscye until the fabric is smooth and the chest and blade fitting lines become level; taper to nothing at the neckline. Mark the new lower position of the armscye seamline to restore armscye depth; blend into the original seamline at the arm hinge areas; attach the sleeves using the new armscye seamlines.

variations.name: Long arm joints (bodice)
variations.figure_analysis: The bones forming the joint structure may be longer than average, or the hinge flesh separating the arm from the rib cage may form farther below the joint than average. Either factor increases the length from the shoulder to the scyeline.
