fitting_analysis: Lower armscye binds against the arm hinges
Diagonal wrinkles pull from the blade and chest areas to the underarms; a fold of fabric may form below the scyeline
Ends of the blade and chest fitting lines may pull downward
variations.fabric_requirement: Increased length of the shoulder joint area needs a longer armscye. This lowers the armscye seamline under the arm and shortens the side seamline. The armscye contour then sits comfortably near the arm hinges. The sleeve cap height must be lengthened (see 73 Long Arm Joints, sleeves).
variations.change_required: Lengthen the depth of the armscye.

methods.slash: If sleeves are attached, see 73 Long Arm Joints (sleeves) and follow that procedure. If sleeves have not been attached, use the pivot method below.
methods.pivot: Clip the seam allowance at ½ inch (1.2 cm) intervals across the underarm area to relieve strain. Mark a new seamline below the original that is a comfortable distance below the arm hinge. Across the side seams, draw a line parallel to the original armscye seamline. Blend into the original seamline at the arm hinge areas on front and back. Trim the excess fabric beyond the new seam allowance.

variations.name: Short arm joints (bodice)
variations.figure_analysis: The bones forming the joint structure may be shorter than average, or the hinge flesh separating the arm from the rib cage may form nearer the joint than average. Either factor decreases the length from the shoulder to the scyeline.
fitting_analysis: The seamline at the lower armscye is too far below the arm hinges
Lifting the arm pulls the sleeves tightly against the arm; the arms cannot be raised comfortably
Blade and chest fitting lines are not affected
variations.fabric_requirement: A shorter shoulder joint area needs a shorter armscye. This raises the armscye seamline nearer the arm and lengthens the side seamline. The strain is relieved on the sleeve. The sleeve cap height must be shortened (see 74 Short Arm Joints, sleeves).
variations.change_required: Shorten the depth of the armscye.

methods.slash: If sleeves are attached, see 74 Short Arm Joints (sleeves) and follow that procedure. If sleeves have not been attached, use the pivot method below.
methods.pivot: At the underarm, mark a new seamline above the original to lift the armscye to a comfortable position. Across the side seams, draw a line parallel to the original armscye seamline. Blend into the original seamline at the arm hinge areas on front and back.

variations.name: Forward arm joints (bodice)
variations.figure_analysis: The collar bones bow forward more than average. This makes the arm joint more rounded in front and flatter at the back; the chest becomes narrower and the blade area broader. Thin muscles and smaller deposits of soft tissue cause indented areas next to the front edges of the arm joints.
fitting_analysis: At the armscye, shoulder seams lie behind the shoulder tips
Garment front forms vertical folds against the arm joints
Back armscye seams pull toward the blade areas
Front sleeve caps are taut near the front of the shoulder crest and loose at the back
variations.fabric_requirement: Forward curvature of the collar bones means the armscye ends of the shoulder seamlines move toward the front. This shortens the front armscye depth and lengthens the back armscye. The narrow chest needs less width in front of the armscyes; the broader upper back needs more width at the upper armscye areas. This variation also changes the contour of the sleeve cap (see 77 Forward Arm Joints, sleeves).
variations.change_required: Widen the blade area and raise the back shoulder seam at the armscye; narrow the chest area and lower the front shoulder seam at the armscye.

methods.slash: Release the sleeve above the arm hinge areas. Slash across the back armscye seam allowances at the arm hinge areas and cut diagonally toward the point of each neckline extension. Insert fabric strips. To increase armscye length, separate the cut edges at the armscye until the shoulderline is in the correct position. Across each front armscye seam allowance at the arm hinge areas, form a diagonal tuck to remove the excess fabric. Adjust the back and front changes until the shoulder seamlines divide the shoulder area evenly. Taper the tucks and slashes to nothing at the neckline extensions. Correct back armscye distortions with a new, straighter seamline from the shoulder tip to the arm hinge area. Correct the front distortion with a curved line through the centre of the distortion. Blend into the original seamline at the lower armscye. For the sleeve cap adjustment, see 77 Forward Arm Joints (sleeves).
methods.pivot: Remove the sleeve cap above the arm hinge areas. Release the shoulder seams for the armscye to the neckline. Extend the seam allowance of the back shoulder toward the front. Turn under the front shoulder seam allowance at the armscye until the fold divides the shoulder and arm evenly; secure the fold to the back shoulder seam allowance. Clip the seam allowance of the front armscye at ½ inch (1.2 cm) intervals along the mid-chest area to relieve strain. Draw a new front armscye seamline even with the crease in the flesh at the arm hinge areas; blend into the original at the shoulder and lower armscye. Let out the back armscye seam allowance at the blade area to form a straighter line; blend into the original seamlines at the shoulder and arm hinge area. For the sleeve cap adjustment, see 77 Forward Arm Joints (sleeves).

variations.name: Prominent collar bones
variations.figure_analysis: The collar bone endings near centre front are larger than average. A bulged area forms at the base of the front neck.
fitting_analysis: Centre front lines on a front closure do not meet

Fabric near the neckline is taut across centre front when the closure is forced to stay closed; extreme variation pulls the vertical fitting lines toward each other at the upper chest and makes the front armscye edges ripple
Neckline and chest fitting lines may rise at centre front
variations.fabric_requirement: The enlarged bone structure below the throat needs more fabric width at the upper centre front. The wider garment area relieves strain and lets the neckline close comfortably and align with the base of the neck; fitting lines become plumb and level.
variations.change_required: Widen and lengthen the upper centre front area.

methods.slash: If the fitting garment has no centre front seam: slash along the centre front line from the neckline seam allowance to the waistline; insert a fabric strip; to increase width, spread the cut edges enough at the neckline to relieve strain and relax the vertical fitting lines; draw a new centre front line down the centre of the fabric insert.
methods.pivot: If the garment has a centre front seamline: let out the seam allowances equally at the neckline to relieve strain and let the centre front lines meet; taper the new centre front lines to nothing at the waistline. If the garment has no centre front seamline: release the shoulder seams and the front of the armscyes from the shoulders down to the point where the strain no longer pulls the sleeve away from the armscye; fold the back shoulder seam allowance under along the shoulder seamline; lay the fold onto the extended front seam allowances, so the front neckline edges move toward the neck; clip as needed to remove strain at the neckline; restitch the shoulder seams; continue the back neckline and armscye seamlines into the original seamlines on the front at the chest area.

variations.name: Prominent sternum / rounded chest
variations.figure_analysis: The upper portion of the sternum is larger than average and protrudes beyond the surface of the ribs. When a rounded chest is present, the chest wall curves outward along the upper centre front. Both reasons for fullness increase the length from the neck to the scyeline area; the width across the chest may increase.
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut at the upper centre front, pulling into diagonal wrinkles from the armscyes to the neckline
Armscyes on a sleeveless dress may ripple at the edges of the chest
Chest fitting line rises at the centre
variations.fabric_requirement: Fullness at the centre of the chest needs more fabric length at the upper centre front. The longer garment area relieves strain at the neckline; the fabric relaxes and the chest fitting line becomes level. More width may be needed at chest level. Armscyes relax and align with the body contours.
variations.change_required: Lengthen and widen the upper centre front.

methods.slash: Slash across the garment front from one armscye to the other, 2 inches (5 cm) below the neckline, following the crosswise grain. Insert a fabric strip. To increase length, spread the cut edges evenly until the chest fitting line is level; taper to nothing at each armscye. If the fabric is taut across the armscyes, follow the pivot method.
methods.pivot: Release the shoulder seams. To increase length, let out the front shoulder seam allowances equally at the neckline until the chest fitting line is level; taper to nothing at each armscye. Raise the neck seamline across the centre front area to restore neckline circumference; blend into the original near each shoulder; restitch the shoulder seams. Check the armscye seamline positions: if they pull toward centre front, let out the armscye seam allowances equally across the chest area to form a straighter armscye line; taper into the original near each shoulder and arm hinge; attach the sleeves using the new armscye seamlines.

variations.name: Hollow chest
variations.figure_analysis: The chest wall is flat or concave. Chest muscle development and soft tissue deposits are minimal. Arm joints appear larger than average; bust curvature appears smaller and lower. The length decreases from the neck to the scyeline area. The width across the chest contour may increase between the shoulder tips. A hollow chest is often combined with a rounded upper back (see 49).
fitting_analysis: Fabric sags into diagonal wrinkles from the shoulder tips to the centre of the chest
Chest fitting line droops at the centre front
variations.fabric_requirement: Shortness of the chest needs less fabric length at the upper centre front. This lets the garment lie smoothly against the chest, and the chest fitting line becomes level.
variations.change_required: Shorten the upper centre front area; widen the area at the shoulder tips.

methods.slash: Below the front neck area, form a parallel tuck wide enough to remove the excess fabric and lift the chest fitting line to a level position. Follow the crosswise grain. Taper to nothing at each armscye.
methods.pivot: Release the shoulder seams. Clip the neck seam allowance across the centre front area. To decrease garment length, take up the front shoulders equally at the neckline until the chest fitting line is level; taper to nothing at each armscye. To restore the neckline, mark a new neckline position across the centre front area; blend into the original near the shoulders. Stitch the shoulder seams using the new front shoulder seamlines.

variations.name: Rounded upper back
variations.figure_analysis: The upper portion of the spine curves outward more than average. The head may rest forward of the central body axis. The length increases from the neck to the mid-blade area. This variation is often combined with a hollow chest (see 48).
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut at the back neckline; strain pulls the neckline below the centre of the neck vertebra
Diagonal wrinkles pull from the armscyes to the upper centre back
Strain pulls the blade fitting line and waistline up at their centres; front neckline may appear too tight
variations.fabric_requirement: The outward contour of the spine needs more fabric length and more fabric shaping at the upper centre back. This relieves strain at the necklines; the blade fitting line and the waistline become level.
variations.change_required: Lengthen the upper centre back area.

methods.slash: Slash across the garment back from one shoulder tip to the other, following the crosswise grain. Insert a fabric strip. To increase garment length at the neckline, spread the cut edges evenly until the blade fitting line is level; taper to nothing at each armscye.
methods.pivot: Release the shoulder seams. Let out the back shoulder seam allowances equally at the neckline until the blade fitting line is level; taper to nothing at the armscyes. This lengthens the shoulder seamline. Widen the shoulder darts to increase garment shaping and restore shoulder seamline length. Draw new shoulder seamlines in straight lines across the widened darts. Mark a new back-neck seamline above the original at centre back equal to the adjustment of the shoulder seamlines. Stitch the shoulder seams using the new back shoulder seamlines.

variations.name: Erect upper back
variations.figure_analysis: The upper portion of the spine curves less than average. The head may rest back of the central body axis. The length decreases from the neck to the mid-blade area. This may result from overly erect posture, and is often combined with a prominent bust or rounded chest (see 64 or 47).
fitting_analysis: Fabric loose over the shoulder blades, sagging into horizontal folds across centre back
Blade fitting line droops at centre back
variations.fabric_requirement: The straighter spine needs less fabric length and less shaping at the upper centre back. This lets the garment lie smoothly against the upper back, and the blade fitting line becomes level.
variations.change_required: Shorten the upper centre back area.

methods.slash: Form a parallel tuck wide enough to lift the blade fitting line to a level position. Follow the crosswise grain. Taper to nothing at each armscye.
methods.pivot: Release the shoulder seams. Take up the shoulder area equally at the back neckline until the blade fitting line is level. Let out the shoulder darts to restore the shoulder seam length. Draw each new shoulder seamline in a straight line across the narrowed dart. Taper to nothing at the armscyes. Mark the lowered neck seamline across centre back equal to the adjustment at the shoulders; blend into the original near each shoulder; trim the excess width from the neckline contour; stitch the shoulder seams using the new back shoulder seamlines.

variations.name: Prominent shoulder blades
variations.figure_analysis: The shoulder blades are larger and protrude more than average. Upper back muscle development and soft tissue deposits may be minimal. The body is recessed along the upper area of the spine. The length and width increase from the centre of each shoulder seamline to the blade line and from armscye to armscye. Asymmetrical figures may have one prominent and one flat blade.
fitting_analysis: Angularity of the shoulder blades pulls tight horizontal wrinkles into the fabric between the blades
Sleeveless armscyes ripple; diagonal wrinkles radiate toward the armscyes at each blade
Sleeve caps pull toward the back; blade fitting line rises
variations.fabric_requirement: Fullness of the shoulder blades needs more fabric width and length and increases shaping. Wider darts result. This relieves strain and lets the armscyes and sleeves align over the arm joints; the blade fitting line becomes level. Armscye size and sleeve need no adjustment.
variations.change_required: Widen and lengthen the area over the blades.

methods.slash: Slash diagonally from each neckline extension to the corresponding armscye at the arm hinge area. Insert fabric strips. To increase width and length, spread the cut edges equally at the dart tips to relax the fabric and restore the ease; taper to nothing at the neckline and the armscyes.
methods.pivot: Release the shoulder and the back armscye seams above the arm hinge areas. Widen the back darts equally until the garment is smooth but relaxed over the shoulder blades and at the armscye; curve and lengthen the darts as needed. Let out the armscye seam allowances to restore the length of the shoulder seamlines. Blend the new armscye into the original at the arm hinge area. Draw each new shoulder seamline in a straight line across the stitched darts.

variations.name: Flat shoulder blades
variations.figure_analysis: The upper portions of the shoulder blades curve outward less than average; the back may appear erect. The width and length decrease from armscye to armscye and from the centre of each shoulder seamline to the blade line, respectively. Asymmetrical figures may have one prominent and one flat blade.
fitting_analysis: Fabric loose over the shoulder blades and may form loose vertical wrinkles
variations.fabric_requirement: A less-curved shoulder blade contour needs less fabric width and length and less dart shaping. The shoulder dart becomes narrower. The smaller garment area lies smoothly against the body.
variations.change_required: Narrow and shorten the area over the blades.

methods.slash: To remove the excess fabric at the tips of the back shoulder darts, form diagonal tucks of equal widths that point toward the neck and underarm. Adjust the tuck widths until the fabric lies smooth; retain sufficient ease; taper to nothing at the neckline and armscyes.
methods.pivot: Release the shoulder seams, the darts and the back armscye seams above the arm hinge areas. Let out the darts equally until the garment is smooth but relaxed over the shoulder blades. Straighten and shorten the darts as needed. Draw new armscye seamlines in the garment area to restore the length of the shoulder seamlines; blend into the original at the arm hinge area. Draw each new shoulder seamline in a straight line across the stitched darts.

variations.name: Broad chest / upper back
variations.figure_analysis: The upper part of the rib cage is fuller than average. The chest or upper back muscle development and soft tissue deposits may be heavier. This increases the width between the arm joints. The structure of the arm joints and arms is not affected.
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut from armscye to armscye, forming tight horizontal wrinkles
Sleeve pulls toward the body centres, causing the armscye to cut against the arm hinge
Vertical fitting line on the sleeve cap bows toward the fullness; chest and blade fitting lines remain level
variations.fabric_requirement: The increased chest or blade span needs more fabric width at the corresponding scyeline and armscyes. This relieves strain at the underarm and chest (blade); sleeves and armscyes relax and align without adjustment.
variations.change_required: Widen the area across the chest or the blades.

methods.slash: About 1 inch (2.5 cm) from each armscye, slash from the shoulderline to the scyeline along the lengthwise grain. Insert fabric strips. To increase width, separate the cut edges equally at the chest or blade line until the armscye lines move to comfortable and attractive positions. Taper to nothing at the shoulders and the scyeline.
methods.pivot: Release the front of the sleeves. Mark the new armscye stitching lines in the seam allowance areas at the edges of the chest (blade) so they lie in comfortable and attractive positions. Taper into the original seamlines near the shoulders and lower armscye curves. Attach the sleeves to the armscyes using the new armscye seamlines.

variations.name: Narrow chest / upper back
variations.figure_analysis: The upper part of the rib cage is smaller than average. Chest or upper back muscle development and soft tissue deposits are minimal; the back may appear erect. The width decreases between the arm joints. The structure of the arm joints and arms is not affected.
fitting_analysis: Fabric loose along the edges of the chest or the blades and at the underarm areas
When the arms move forward, the front armscyes cut against the arm hinges
When the arms are lifted, sleeves pull against the arm and restrict movement; chest and blade fitting lines remain level
variations.fabric_requirement: A decreased chest or blade span needs less fabric width at the corresponding scyeline and armscyes. This lets the garment lie smoothly and comfortably against the rib cage; sleeves align without adjustment.
variations.change_required: Narrow the area across the chest or the blade.

methods.slash: About 1 inch (2.5 cm) from each armscye, form a vertical tuck to remove the excess fabric. Adjust the widths equally until the garment area is smooth; retain sufficient ease at the blade line. Taper the ends of the tucks to nothing near the shoulders and the scyeline.
methods.pivot: Mark new armscye seamlines in the garment area at the edges of the chest (blade) so they lie in comfortable and attractive positions. Taper into the original seamlines near the shoulder and the lower armscye curves. If the sleeves have been set in, release the front (back) areas from the shoulders to the underarm areas and proceed as stated above. Attach the sleeves to the armscyes using the new armscye seamlines.

variations.name: Wide rib cage
variations.figure_analysis: The midsection of the rib cage is fuller than average and increases the body circumference at the scye line. The side of the rib cage tapers more than average. This lengthens the side of the body between the base of the arm joints and the waist. Chest and blade fitting lines remain level; arm joints and arms are not affected.
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut under each arm, forming tight wrinkles that follow the curves of the armscye seamlines
Tightness makes the armscyes appear too tight and the bust area of the garment appear too small
variations.fabric_requirement: The increased rib cage circumference needs more fabric width at the scyeline. This relieves strain and restores ease in the garment at the underarm areas; armscyes align with the body contour. The adjustment may be needed on the back, the front, or both.
variations.change_required: Widen the area near the underarm extension.

methods.slash: Slash from the mid-armscye to the waistline, following the lengthwise grain. Insert fabric strips. To increase width, spread the cut edges equally at the scyeline to relieve the tension and restore the ease. Taper the end of each slash to nothing at the armscye and waistline.
methods.pivot: Release the side seams and the lower armscye seams up to the corresponding blade or chest area. Let out the side seam allowances equally at the scyeline to relieve the tension and restore the ease. Restore the armscye seamline from the new side seam position to the original at the blade or chest area. Draw a new side seam in a straight line from the new position at the underarm to the original at the waistline. Repeat on the front as needed.

variations.name: Narrow rib cage
variations.figure_analysis: The midsection of the rib cage is narrower than average and decreases the body circumference at the scyeline. The upper torso area tapers less than average. This shortens the side of the body between the base of the arm joints and the waist. Chest and blade fitting lines remain level.
fitting_analysis: Fabric near the lower armscye hangs in vertical folds near the armscyes on front and back
Excess garment width inhibits arm movement; the front armscye cuts against the arm hinge
Sleeves appear too tight when the arms are lifted
variations.fabric_requirement: A decreased rib cage circumference needs less fabric width at the scyeline. This permits the armscyes to align with the body contour and the arm to move without constraint or discomfort. The adjustment may be needed on the back, the front, or both.
variations.change_required: Narrow the area near the underarm extension.

methods.slash: Below the vertical portion of the armscyes, form vertical tucks of equal widths at the scyeline. Adjust the widths equally until the excess fabric is removed; retain sufficient ease. Taper the tucks to nothing at the armscye and the waistline.
methods.pivot: Release the side seams and the lower armscye seams to the corresponding blade or chest area. At the scyeline, take in the side garment areas equally until the excess fabric is removed; retain sufficient ease. Restore the armscye seamline from the new side seam position to the original at the blade or chest area. Draw a new side seam in a straight line from the new position at the underarm to the original at the waistline. Repeat on the front as needed.

variations.name: Cylindrical-shaped torso (rib cage)
variations.figure_analysis: The rib cage is rounder than average. The torso is deeper from centre front through to centre back. The bone structures forming the arm joints may also be larger than average. These factors increase body depth from the front arm hinge to that at the back.
fitting_analysis: Armscye cuts against the arm hinges
Diagonal wrinkles pull from the blade and chest areas to the underarm; a fold of fabric forms below the scyeline
Sleeves pull at the underarm and may be too tight around the arm; armscye seamlines pull toward the arm at front and back
variations.fabric_requirement: Greater profile depth needs more fabric width at the underarm area on both sleeve and garment. More armscye length may also be needed at the shoulder. The wider armscye extensions on the garment and sleeve let the fabric relax underneath the arms and around the torso; armscyes relax and align along the blade and chest.
variations.change_required: Widen the armscye extension.

methods.slash: Near each side seam, slash the garment from the armscye to the waistline on both front and back. Insert fabric strips. To increase width, spread each set of cut edges equally at the scyeline to relax the fabric and restore the ease. Taper to nothing at the waistline. For the sleeve adjustment, see 75 Large Shoulder Joints and 80 Large Upper Arms.
methods.pivot: Release the side seams and the lower armscye area if the sleeves are attached. At the scyeline, let out both front and back seam allowances equally to relax the fabric and restore the ease. Taper to nothing at the waistline. For the sleeve adjustment, see 75 Large Shoulder Joints and 80 Large Upper Arms.

variations.name: Oval-shaped torso (rib cage)
variations.figure_analysis: The rib cage is more oval than average. The torso is narrower from centre front through to centre back. The bone structures forming the arm joints may be smaller than average. These factors decrease body depth from the front arm hinge to that at the back.
fitting_analysis: Garment hangs in loose vertical folds near the underarm on both front and back
Sleeve appears too large; when the arms are raised, strain pulls the sleeves tightly against the arm and the arms cannot be raised comfortably
variations.fabric_requirement: Smaller profile depth needs less fabric width at the underarm area on sleeve and garment. Less armscye length may also be needed at the shoulder. The narrower armscye extensions on garment and sleeve bring the fabric closer to the body; arms can be raised easily and comfortably.
variations.change_required: Narrow the armscye extension.

methods.slash: Near each side seam, form a vertical tuck at the scyeline on both front and back. Adjust the widths equally until the excess fabric is removed but the ease is retained. Taper the tucks to nothing at the waistline. For the sleeve adjustment, see 76 Small Shoulder Joints and 79 Thin Arms.
methods.pivot: Release the side seams and the lower armscye area if the sleeves are attached. At the scyeline, take in the garment areas equally until the excess fabric is removed; retain sufficient ease. Taper into the original at the waistline. For the sleeve adjustment, see 76 Small Shoulder Joints and 79 Thin Arms.

variations.name: Long upper rib cage
variations.figure_analysis: The bones forming the upper rib cage are heavier than average. The spacing between adjacent ribs may be greater. The length increases from the shoulder to the bustline. This variation may affect the space between the arm hinge or the length of the arm joints.
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut between the shoulder seams and the waistline, may form tight vertical wrinkles
Darted area too high, creating the illusion of a low bust position
Midriff and waistline rise onto larger body areas and appear too small; armscye may cut against the arm hinge; chest and blade fitting lines remain level
variations.fabric_requirement: Longer rib cage areas need more fabric length between the shoulder seams and the bustline. This relieves strain at the chest and upper back. The garment shaping, the midriff and the waistline lower and align with the body contours.
variations.change_required: Lengthen the appropriate area between the shoulder area and the bustline.

methods.slash: If the armscye pulls against the arm hinge, cut across the front and back of the garment through the armscye, following the crosswise grain; insert fabric strips; separate each set of cut edges evenly until the armscye seamline lowers to a comfortable position. The length adjustment may not be equal on front and back. If the armscye length is correct but the garment shaping is too high, slash completely around the garment about 1 inch (2.5 cm) below the scyeline, following the crosswise grain; insert a strip; spread the cut edges evenly until garment shaping and waistline align with the bust and waist. If the armscye and centre front lengths are correct but the shaping is too full and the centre back too short, lengthen only the back: release side seams across the side dart area and the side darts, cut across the back at the bustline, insert a strip, separate evenly until the strain is relieved and the waistline is level; let out dart width as needed; for extra front length let out the front waistline seam evenly; true the side seams. See 66 Small Bust.
methods.pivot: If the armscye cuts against the arm hinge: release the shoulder seams; let out back and front seam allowances evenly on each shoulder until the lower armscye seamline lowers to a comfortable position; adjust the length change parallel to the original seamlines until the garment lies smooth but relaxed over chest and blade. Restore the depth of back and front necklines: raise the neckline at centre front and centre back by the length adjustment at the shoulders; blend into the original near the shoulders. If the armscye length is correct but shaping and waistline are too high: release side seam, underarm dart and waistline seam; move the underarm dart down to the fullest part of the bust; shorten back and front waistline darts equal to the side dart adjustment; mark the new waistline parallel to the original; restore waist circumferences; remark and restitch the underarm seamlines. Princess style: release seams across the bust area; reshape the side panel so the greatest curvature is at the bustline; correct the waistline as above. If only the back is too short and the dart shaping too large: release side seams and side darts; narrow the darts until shaping is correct; trace the side seamlines straight across the closed darts; stitch the side seams; mark the new back waistline even with the front. See 66 Small Bust.

variations.name: Short upper rib cage
variations.figure_analysis: The bones forming the upper rib cage are lighter than average; the spacing between adjacent ribs may be closer. The length decreases from the shoulder to the bustline. This variation may affect the length of the joints or the space between the arm hinge and the bustline.
fitting_analysis: Fabric sags into a loose horizontal fold at the bustline or near the waistline

Armscye may drop too far below the arm hinge; darted area too low, creating the illusion of a high bust; midriff lowers into the smaller body area and appears too large; chest and blade fitting lines remain level
variations.fabric_requirement: Shorter rib cage areas need less fabric length between the shoulder seams and the bustline. This lets the garment lie smoothly against the chest and upper back; garment shaping, the midriff and the waistline align with the body contours.
variations.change_required: Shorten the appropriate area between the shoulder and the bustline.

methods.slash: If the armscye drops too far below the arm hinge, make a parallel tuck across the garment at the chest and blade lines, following the crosswise grain; adjust the size of each tuck until the armscye seamline rises to a comfortable position; the length adjustment may not be equal on front and back. If the armscye length is correct but the shaping is too low, form a parallel tuck completely around the garment about 1 inch (2.5 cm) below the scyeline, following the crosswise grain; adjust the tuck width evenly to lift the underarm dart into the correct position. If the armscye and centre front lengths are correct but the shaping is too small and the centre back too long, shorten only the back: release side seams; make a parallel tuck completely across the back area at the bustline to remove the excess fabric length; widen the dart equal to the length adjustment; true the side seams with straight lines across the adjustment. See 65 Large Bust.
methods.pivot: If the armscye drops too far below the arm hinge: release the shoulder seams; clip the front neck seam allowance across centre front; take up both front and back shoulder seam areas evenly until the lower armscye seamline rises to a comfortable position; adjust the length change parallel to the original seamlines until the garment lies smooth but relaxed over chest and blade. Lower the neckline seam at centre front and centre back by the length adjustment at the shoulders; blend into the original at the shoulder areas. If the armscye length is correct but shaping and waistline are too low: release side seams, underarm darts and waistline; move the underarm darts up to align with the fullest part of the bust; lengthen back and front waistline darts equal to the side dart adjustment; mark the new waistline parallel to the original; restore waistline circumferences; remark and stitch the new underarm seamlines. Princess style: release seams across the bust area; reshape the side panel so the greatest curvature is at the bustline; correct the waistline as above. If only the back is too long but the dart shaping too small: release the side seams and side darts; widen the darts until shaping is correct; mark a new front side seam in a straight line across the closed dart; stitch the side seams; mark the new back waistline even with that of the front. See 65 Large Bust.

variations.name: High bust position
variations.figure_analysis: When associated with the youthful figure, the bust level is higher than in the mature figure because breast tissue is still firm, taut and rounded. For other figures the bust contour is higher than average. Erect posture and bras with tight straps or firm support under the cups also raise the crest of the bust fullness. The distance from the shoulders to the bustline is shorter than average; the distance from the bustline to the waist is greater.
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut across the fullest area of the bust but loose underneath, because fabric shaping lies below the bust contour
Bust fitting line remains level
variations.fabric_requirement: Changing length above and below the crest of the bust requires raising the tip of the side dart and lengthening the front waist darts. The adjusted dart tips let the fabric shaping align with the bust contour.
variations.change_required: Raise the tips of all the bust darts.

methods.slash: Only the dart stitching line positions are affected. Use the pivot procedure.
methods.pivot: Mark the position for the new underarm dart tips directly above those of the original darts. Release the side seams and the underarm darts. Form new dart centre folds between the new dart tip mark and the place where the original fold meets the side seamline. Stitch each new dart straight from the new tip to the original dartline marking at the side seamline. True the distorted side seamline in a straight line across the closed dart; draw from the original side seam markings at the armscye and waistline; stitch the side seams. Lengthen each waist dart by an amount equal to the adjustment at the underarm dart tip. Princess style: release the seamline across the bust area; let out the side panel seam allowance at the bust level enough to relax the fabric and restore the ease; take in the side panel below bust level to remove the excess; blend into the original seamline above and below the bust area; stitch.

variations.name: Low or pendulous bust position
variations.figure_analysis: When associated with the mature figure, the fullness of the breast tissues rests below the area of origin because the connective tissues have lost tone. For other figures, the bust contour is lower than average. Slumped posture emphasises and contributes to a lowered bust contour. The distance from the shoulders to the bustline is greater than average; the distance from the bustline to the waist is less. Properly fitted bras with adequate support minimise the variation.
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut across the fullest area of the bust but loose above it, because fabric shaping is above the crest of the bust contour
Tight horizontal wrinkles pull across the waist dartlines; bust fitting line remains level
variations.fabric_requirement: The change in length above and below the crest of the bust requires lowering the side darts and shortening the waistline darts so the fabric shaping aligns with the bust contour.
variations.change_required: Lower the side bust darts parallel to the original; lower the tips of the waistline darts.

methods.slash: Only the dart stitching line positions are affected. Use the procedure indicated for the pivot method.
methods.pivot: Mark the position for new underarm dart tips directly below those of the original darts. Release the side seams across the underarm darts; release the underarm darts. To form the new centre folds, begin at the new tip mark and fold the fabric parallel to the original folds. At the side seamlines, mark the dart width equal to the original width of the folded dart; stitch the new darts; true the distorted side seamline in a straight line across the closed dart; stitch the side seams. Release the waistline seam across the waistline darts; shorten each waistline dart by an amount equal to the adjustment at the underarm dart tips; retain the dart width; stitch the new darts; remove the original dart stitching; stitch the waistline seam. Princess style: release the seamline across the bust area; at bust level let out the side panel enough to relax the fabric and restore the ease; take in the side panel enough above bust level to remove the excess; blend smoothly into the original seamline above and below the bust area; stitch.

variations.name: Wide bust point span
variations.figure_analysis: The breast contours develop further from the sternum than average. This increases the span between the bust points and decreases the measurement from the bust points to the sides of the body.
fitting_analysis: Waistline dart tips point toward the centre edges of the bust, so fabric shaping is too near centre front; horizontal wrinkles may form across centre front at bust level
Underarm dartlines extend onto the bust curvature instead of ending along the side edges; this causes tight vertical wrinkles across these darts
Bust fitting line remains level
variations.fabric_requirement: The wider space between bust points needs waist dart tips to end farther from centre front. The figure may need the slope of the waist darts changed, or the entire dart moved farther from centre front. The narrow side areas need shorter underarm darts.
variations.change_required: Reposition the waistline darts to align the dart tips with the bust points; shorten the underarm darts.

methods.slash: Only the dart stitching line positions are affected. Use the procedure indicated for the pivot method.
methods.pivot: Mark the new dart tip positions in the correct location toward the side of the original dart tips. Release the waist and side seamlines across the dart areas; release the waistline darts. For each waistline dart, form a new centre fold from the new tip mark to the place where the original centre fold meets the waistline; stitch the new darts from the tip to the waistline; the waistline edges will no longer be even. The entire dart position may be moved toward the side instead. Shorten the underarm darts: retain the original centre folds and stitch straight from the new tip mark to the original dart stitching lines at the side seam. True the side seamlines with a straight line across the closed darts; stitch the side seams and the waist seam.

variations.name: Prominent bust
variations.figure_analysis: The person assumes an erect stance with an upward, forward thrust to the rib cage. Breast tissues form a lifted, conical contour. The bust contour may be prominent regardless of cup size. If the cup size is a C or larger, the front measurements at bust level increase in length, width and depth.
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut across the fullest area of the bust because fabric shaping is too low
If the cup size is C or larger, the front of the garment is too short and too narrow
Diagonal wrinkles radiate from the bust curves to the garment edges; buttoned front closures gap at bust level; bust fitting line rises across the centre front area
Lower edges of an unfastened front closure overlap; waist and hemlines on loosely fitted garments rise at centre front
variations.fabric_requirement: The lift of the bust contour requires raising the front dart tip positions. Figures with a cup size larger than B need more width and length at bust level, which means wider, longer darts. The adjusted garment lies smooth but relaxed and aligns with the body; the lower edges become level and the closure edges lie plumb.
variations.change_required: Widen and lengthen the front at the bustline as necessary; lengthen the front darts.

methods.slash: To add width, slash the garment front from the armscye to the waistline near each side seam. Insert fabric strips. Separate each set of cut edges evenly to relax the fabric and restore the ease at the bustline. True the armscye seamline across the adjustment. Restore the armscye size with a dart in each lower armscye area; taper to nothing at the underarm dart tips. To add length, slash across the front just below the underarm dartlines, following the crosswise grain; insert fabric strips; between the waist dart tips, separate the cut edges evenly until the waistline becomes level; taper to nothing at the side seams; mark the new position for the waist dart tips if they require lengthening. To restore the waistline size, release the waistline from the dart to the side insert; remove the waist dart stitching; widen each dart at the side dartline to absorb the width adjustment at the side seam; move the dart tip toward the side by one half of this amount; stitch the new darts from the tip to the waistline. True the distorted seamline contour in the lower armscye area and across the waist dart areas; stitch the waistline.
methods.pivot: Adjust for width first. Release the side seams. Let out the front seam allowances equally at the bustline as needed to relax the fabric and restore the ease over the bust. Mark the new side seamline position at each underarm dart. Widen the underarm darts equally until the fabric lies smooth but relaxed at the edge of the bust area; retain the original dart centre folds. Draw each new side seamline parallel to the original from the waistline through the armscye seam allowance; restore the length of the side seamline by measuring equal distances into the armscye and waistline seam allowances; mark the ends of the seamline at the waistline and armscyes. Draw new armscye seamlines from the original seamline at the arm hinge area to the end of the new side seamline. To restore the waistline size, release the front waistline and the waistline darts; widen each waist dart at the side dartline to absorb the width adjustment at the side seam; move the dart tip toward the side by one half the dart width adjustment; stitch the darts. Draw the new waistline parallel to the original at centre front and side seam areas, in a smooth curve across the darts; stitch the side seamlines and the waistline seam. Length is added by the slash method above.

variations.name: Large bust
variations.figure_analysis: The bust development is larger than average (a B cup); the circumference at the bustline is greater. There is no relationship between muscle and frame size and bust development, but excess fatty tissue may accumulate in the breast tissues also.
fitting_analysis: Fabric taut at the bustline, which draws attention to the amount of bust development
Diagonal wrinkles radiate from the bust curves to the garment edges and centre front; deep ripples form at the armscyes making them appear too large
Buttoned front closures gap at bust level; underarm dart pulls onto the bust curvature; front waist and hemlines raise the lower edges of unfastened closures; bust fitting line remains level
variations.fabric_requirement: The larger bust circumference needs more fabric width at the bustline, so front darts become wider. The larger garment area and fuller shaping relax over the bust; lower edges become level and the centre front edges lie plumb. Armscye size does not increase even though the shape changes; the armscye size is set by the arm joint structure and rib cage depth.
variations.change_required: Widen the front at the bustline.

methods.slash: Near each side seam, slash the garment front from the armscye to the waistline. Insert fabric strips. To increase width, separate each set of cut edges evenly to relax the fabric and restore the ease at the bustline. Mark new underarm dart tip positions, if necessary. Restore the armscye size with a dart in each lower armscye area; taper to nothing at the new underarm dart tip positions; true the armscye across the adjustment.
methods.pivot: Adjust for width first. Release the side seams. Let out the front seam allowances equally at the bustline as needed to relax the fabric and restore the ease over the bust. Mark the new side seamline position at the underarm dart. Release the underarm darts and widen them equally at the upper dartline until the fabric lies smooth but relaxed at the edge of the bust area. Draw each new side seamline in a straight line parallel to the original from the waistline to the armscye seam allowances; restore the length of the side seamline by measuring from the waistline into the armscye; mark the ends at the armscyes. Draw new armscye seamlines from the original seamline at the arm hinge area to the end of the new side seamline. To restore the waistline size, release the front waistline and the waistline dart; widen each waistline dart at the side dartline to absorb the width adjustment at the side seam; move the dart tip toward the side by one half the dart width adjustment; stitch the darts; true the waistline across the adjusted darts; stitch the side seamlines and waistline seam. For a C or larger cup, where the centre front is correct but the centre back is too long: shorten only the back. Release the side seams; make a parallel tuck completely across the back area at the bustline to remove the excess length; widen the dart equal to the length adjustment; true side seams in straight lines across the adjustments.

variations.name: Small bust
variations.figure_analysis: The bust development is less than average (below a B cup); the circumference at the bustline is smaller. There is no relationship between muscle and frame size and bust development.
fitting_analysis: Garment too loose at the bustline, which draws attention to the smallness of the contour
Loose vertical folds across the underarm dart; bust fitting line may droop at centre front
Loose horizontal fold may form underneath the bust; lower edges of unfastened closures spread apart; front waist and hemlines droop
A padded B-cup bra may eliminate the need for garment adjustment
variations.fabric_requirement: The smaller bust circumference needs less fabric width at the bustline, and less length may be needed at centre front at bust level. Narrower darts result. The smaller garment area lies smoothly against the body; the bust fitting line and lower edges become level; closure edges lie plumb. Armscye size does not decrease although the shape changes; the armscye size is set by arm joint structure and rib cage depth.
variations.change_required: Narrow the front at the bustline; shorten the front, if necessary.

methods.slash: Near each side seam, form a vertical parallel tuck on the garment front. Adjust the tuck widths equally until the fabric is smooth but relaxed at the bustline. Continue the tucks an even width to the armscye and the waistline. Mark new underarm dart tip positions, if necessary. To restore the armscye size, slash through the lower armscye area, continuing to the new tip of each underarm dart; insert fabric strips; separate each set of cut edges equally at the armscye to gain an amount of width equal to the adjustment at the side seam area; true the armscye across the adjustment.
methods.pivot: Adjust for width first. Release the side seams. Take in the side seam areas equally at the bustline to remove the excess fabric; retain sufficient ease over the bust. Mark the new side seamline position at the underarm dart. To correct the length, release the underarm darts; narrow both darts equally at the upper dartlines until the fabric lies smooth but relaxed at the armscye areas. Draw each new side seamline in a straight line parallel to the original from the waistline to the armscye seamlines. To restore the waistline size, release the front waistline and the waistline darts; narrow each waistline dart at the side dartlines to let out the width taken up at the side seam; move the dart tip toward the centre by one half the dart width adjustment; stitch the darts; raise the waistline seam if needed; shorten the back an equal amount; true the waistline across the adjusted darts. Restore the length of each side seamline by measuring from the new waistline toward the armscye; mark the end at the armscye areas. Draw new armscye seamlines from the original seamline at the arm hinge area to the end of the new side seamline; stitch the side seams and the waistline seam.

variations.name: Flared lower ribs
variations.figure_analysis: The front of the rib cage slopes outward excessively from the chest to the lower edge. The lower rib contour protrudes more than average and increases the torso circumference at that level. The area over the diaphragm may be recessed.
fitting_analysis: Garment taut across the lower edge of the rib cage; at centre front the fabric forms tight horizontal wrinkles
Strain causes the waist dartlines to curve toward each other
variations.fabric_requirement: The fullness at the lower edge of the rib cage needs more fabric width at the midfront areas. The waist darts are sewn in straight rather than curved lines. The increase in garment width relieves the strain and relaxes the fabric.
variations.change_required: Release width from the front waistline darts.

methods.slash: Not appropriate, because only the dartline contours can be adjusted. Use the pivot procedure.
methods.pivot: Release the waist seam across the front waistline darts. Put on the garment and let out both darts until the darts and the fabric relax. Stitch the darts and the waistline.

variations.name: Long midriff
variations.figure_analysis: The lower ribs and vertebrae may be heavier than average. The spacing between the ribs may be greater, or the spine may be longer than average in the area between the waist and the lower rib cage. These factors increase body length between the waist and the bust and blade areas.
fitting_analysis: Garment taut at the waistline; fabric forms tight horizontal wrinkles because the garment waistline lies above the waist level of the body
A higher waistline on a jacket or semi-fitted garment cut in one piece with the skirt may create unattractive body proportions
variations.fabric_requirement: The longer midriff area needs more fabric length between the waistline and the lower edges of the bust and blade contours. The longer garment area lets the fabric relax, and the waistline aligns with the contour of the body at the waist.
variations.change_required: Lengthen the midriff.

methods.slash: Slash around the entire garment near the waistline. Insert fabric strips. To increase length, separate the cut edges evenly around the garment until the waistline aligns with the waist contour.
methods.pivot: Release the entire waistline and side seams. Mark the correct waistline position in the seam allowance across centre front. Continue the new waist seamline parallel to the original completely around the garment. Extend each end of the back and front waistlines equally into the side seam allowances to restore the waistline measurements. Mark each new side seamline from the original at the armscyes to the mark on the new waistline. Stitch the side seams and the waist seam.

variations.name: Short midriff
variations.figure_analysis: The lower ribs and vertebrae may be lighter than average. The spacing between the ribs may be less, or the spine may be shorter than average in the area between the waist and the lower rib cage. These factors decrease body length between the waist and the bust and blade areas.
fitting_analysis: Fabric sags around the waistline area and forms a loose horizontal fold at the waistline
Lower waistline position on jackets and semi-fitted garments cut in one with the skirt drops below waist level and may create unattractive proportions
variations.fabric_requirement: The shorter midriff area needs less fabric length between the waistline and the lower edges of the bust and blade contours. The shorter midriff of the garment fits smoothly against the body; the waistline of loosely fitted garments aligns with the body contour at the waist.
variations.change_required: Shorten the midriff.

methods.slash: Form a parallel tuck near the waistline completely around the garment. Adjust the width of the tuck until the waistline seam aligns with the waist contour. When stitching the tuck, place the waistline area of the garment uppermost on the machine.
methods.pivot: Release the entire waistline and side seams. Mark the correct waistline position across centre front. Continue the new waist seamline parallel to the original completely around the garment. Mark the ends of the new waist seamline at the side seam areas to restore the waistline measurements. Mark each new side seamline from the original at the armscyes to the mark on the new waistline. Stitch the side seams and the waist seam.

variations.name: Large waist
variations.figure_analysis: The body indents very little at the waist, either because the muscles lack tone, the posture is slumped, or the soft tissue deposits are larger than average in that area. The waist circumference is more nearly equal to that of the rib cage and the hips. The sides of the body are straighter and measure slightly shorter than average from the base of the arm joints to the waist.
fitting_analysis: Fabric pulls into taut horizontal wrinkles near the waist
Garment waistline may rise; bodice may appear too long
Lengthwise ease cannot distribute itself properly below the bust level
variations.fabric_requirement: The larger waist circumference needs more fabric width at the waistline. The wider garment area relaxes; the waistline lowers and aligns with the contour of the body.
variations.change_required: Widen the side seam area at the waistline.

methods.slash: Near the side seams, slash through the waistline on the back and front of the garment. Continue cutting to the armscye seamlines. Insert fabric strips. To increase width, separate each set of cut edges equally at the waistline to relax the garment and restore the ease. Taper to nothing at the armscye.
methods.pivot: Release the side seams. Let out equal amounts on the front and back at the waistline on both side seams to relax the fabric and restore the ease. Taper each new side seamline straight from the original at the armscye to the new waistline position. Stitch the new side seams.

variations.name: Small waist
variations.figure_analysis: The body indents more than average at the waist, either because the muscles are more taut, the posture is overly erect, or the soft tissue deposits are smaller than average. The waist circumference is noticeably less than that of the rib cage or the hips. The indentation defines the hourglass figure type. The sides of the body are more sloped and measure slightly longer than average from the base of the arm joints to the waist.
fitting_analysis: Garment baggy around the waist; fabric at the waistline forms loose vertical folds
variations.fabric_requirement: The smaller waist circumference needs less fabric width at the waistline. The narrower garment area lies closer to the body.
variations.change_required: Narrow the side area at the waistline.

methods.slash: Form tucks of equal width through the waistline on the back and front near the side seams. Adjust the tucks equally until the excess fabric is removed and the ease is retained. Taper each tuck to nothing at the armscye seamline.
methods.pivot: Release the side seams. Take in equal amounts on the front and back at the waistline on both side seams until the fabric is smooth and the ease is retained. Taper each new side seamline straight from the original at the armscye to the new waistline position.

variations.name: Arm length variations
variations.figure_analysis: The elbow position determines upper and lower arm length variations. The lengths of the upper and lower arm bone areas develop independently. The total arm length may be average while the upper area is shorter and the lower longer, or vice versa. The variation may occur in the upper arm, the lower arm, or both.
fitting_analysis: Centre of the darted or eased sleeve area should align with the elbow point. When the dart shaping rises above the elbow, the narrower lower sleeve lies over the elbow and restricts mobility
When the shaping drops below the elbow level, the larger upper sleeve lies over the elbow and the sleeve may appear too big
Long sleeve hemline above the wristbone looks uncomfortably short; hemline below the wristbone makes sleeves drag
variations.fabric_requirement: A longer upper arm needs more fabric length between the scyeline and the elbow line; a shorter upper arm needs less. A longer lower arm needs more fabric below the elbow; a shorter lower arm needs less. When both areas vary, changes are needed above and below the elbow line. Aligning the centre of the darted area with the elbow permits elbow movement; aligning the hemline with the wristbone gives comfortable proportions.
variations.change_required: Adjust the lengths of the upper and lower sleeve areas so that the elbow line crosses the elbow point and the wristline is near the wristbone.
